paths.title: Prepare infrastructure for devices using Microsoft Intune and Microsoft Entra ID
paths.summary: Learn how to configure Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft Intune to support modern endpoint management. This learning path covers identity infrastructure, device enrollment, and automated deployment strategies for Windows, iOS/iPadOS, macOS, and Android devices.

modules.title: Understand endpoint management strategies and Microsoft Intune
modules.learnSummary: Introduces Microsoft Intune, management models (cloud-only, hybrid, co-managed), and how Microsoft Entra ID supports device management.
modules.tldr: Intune is Microsoft's cloud service for managing devices (MDM) and protecting data inside apps (MAM). Microsoft Entra ID supplies the user, group and device identities that every Intune assignment depends on. Pick a management model — cloud-only, hybrid or co-managed — based on your existing infrastructure and migration goals.
objectives: Describe how Microsoft Intune works as a cloud-based device management service
Compare Configuration Manager, Intune and co-management
Explain the role of Microsoft Entra ID in Intune-based device management
Evaluate cloud-only, hybrid and co-managed device management models
Identify the key MDM capabilities in Intune
keyPoints: **MDM** manages the whole device (settings, updates, security, inventory); **MAM** protects corporate data inside apps and also works on devices that are **not enrolled** — ideal for BYOD.
Policies are created in the **Intune admin center**, assigned to **Entra ID groups**, and delivered to devices over **HTTPS** — no VPN or on-premises servers needed.
Intune **can't work without Microsoft Entra ID**: enrollment starts with Entra authentication and creates a device object Intune references.

Three join types: **Entra registered** (BYOD, light management via app protection), **Entra joined** (cloud-only corporate, full MDM), **hybrid Entra joined** (also in on-prem AD, enables co-management).
**Co-management** = one Windows device managed by Configuration Manager *and* Intune; you move **workloads** (e.g. compliance, Windows Update policies) to Intune one at a time.
**RBAC** limits what each admin sees and can do — e.g. help desk can wipe a lost device without seeing licensing.
Intune supports the full device lifecycle: **provision → configure → secure → monitor → retire**.

units.title: What is Microsoft Intune and how does it work?
points: Cloud service: configuration and policy definitions live in the cloud; devices check in over the internet.
MDM controls the device; MAM protects data in apps, also on unenrolled devices. Many organizations combine both (corporate phones enrolled, personal tablets app protection only).
On enrollment the device registers and downloads a management profile that establishes trust.
Intune tracks compliance, reports inventory and can run remote actions such as lock or wipe.
Typical roles: Global Administrator, Intune Administrator (no billing/licensing), and a compliance-focused admin role; RBAC narrows permissions per job.

units.title: Compare Configuration Manager, Intune, and co-management
points: Configuration Manager: on-premises, Windows-focused, deep inventory and scripting, works offline — but needs servers and bandwidth.
Intune: cloud, multi-platform (Windows, macOS, iOS/iPadOS, Android), modern app types (Win32, MSIX, Store) — less granular inventory, needs internet.
Co-management: Windows 10/11 only; phased migration per workload; extra complexity of dual management.
To start: enroll a Configuration Manager–managed device in Intune, then in the Configuration Manager console choose which workloads Intune controls.

units.title: Understand the role of Microsoft Entra ID in Intune
points: Every Intune assignment is identity-based: users, groups and devices come from Entra ID.
The device object records type, ownership and join type.
Entra ID issues the tokens; Conditional Access combines identity with device compliance from Intune before granting access.

units.title: Evaluate device management models
points: **Cloud-only**: devices Entra joined, all policy from Intune — for cloud-first, remote/mobile and BYOD scenarios.
**Hybrid**: devices joined to on-prem AD and hybrid Entra joined; Group Policy and Intune side by side — for legacy apps that need domain authentication.
**Co-managed**: Configuration Manager and Intune together, shifting workloads gradually — for heavy Configuration Manager users.
You can start with one model and evolve as the organization changes.

units.title: Explore MDM capabilities in Intune
points: Enrollment and provisioning: Autopilot, Apple automated enrollment, or manual enrollment; zero-touch setup reduces hands-on work.
Configuration profiles set device settings; security baselines give recommended settings; compliance policies check requirements and can flag or block non-compliant devices.
App deployment (store, line-of-business, web apps), monitoring and reporting dashboards, and remote actions (lock, wipe, reset).

keyTerms.definition: Mobile device management — settings and policies applied to an enrolled device.
Mobile application management — protects corporate data inside apps; works without enrollment.
Configuration Manager and Intune manage the same Windows device; workloads are switched to Intune individually.
A management area (e.g. compliance policies, Windows Update policies) assigned to either Configuration Manager or Intune under co-management.

keyTerms.term: Microsoft Entra registered / joined / hybrid joined
keyTerms.definition: The three device identity types: personal (BYOD), cloud-only corporate, and on-prem AD–joined with a cloud identity.

tables.title: Which management model?
rows: Cloud-first, remote workforce, minimal on-prem infrastructure, BYOD
Hybrid Microsoft Entra joined (on-prem AD + Entra)
Existing AD investment, legacy apps needing domain authentication, Group Policy still required
Large Configuration Manager estates migrating workload by workload

remember: BYOD without enrollment → think **MAM / app protection policies**, not MDM.
Co-management is **Windows only**; macOS, iOS/iPadOS and Android are managed by Intune alone.
Intune policies target **Entra ID groups** — no group, no assignment.

selfCheck.q: Employees want to read company email on their personal phones without enrolling them. Which Intune approach fits?
selfCheck.a: MAM — app protection policies protect the corporate data in the apps without enrolling the device.

selfCheck.q: A company manages 10,000 laptops with Configuration Manager and wants to move compliance to the cloud first. What do they enable?
selfCheck.a: Co-management, switching the compliance policies workload to Intune while Configuration Manager keeps the rest.

selfCheck.q: Which device join type is used for cloud-only corporate devices with full MDM?
selfCheck.a: Microsoft Entra joined.

modules.title: Configure Microsoft Entra ID for device and policy management
modules.learnSummary: Configure user and device identity, admin roles, registration settings, and dynamic groups to support Intune policy targeting.
modules.tldr: Microsoft Entra ID is the identity foundation for Intune: it authenticates users, holds device records and provides the groups you use to target policies. You prepare it by building a clean user and group structure, delegating least-privilege admin roles, and setting device registration and join options. Dynamic groups keep policy targeting accurate automatically, based on user or device attributes.
objectives: Explain how Microsoft Entra ID provides the identity infrastructure for Intune device management
Create and manage user accounts and groups in Microsoft Entra ID
Assign appropriate administrative roles for device management tasks
Configure device registration settings to control how devices join Microsoft Entra ID
Create dynamic membership groups using rules based on user or device attributes
keyPoints: Every enrolling user and every device accessing resources needs an **identity in Microsoft Entra ID**; Entra groups decide which users and devices get which Intune policies.
Use **security groups** for Intune policy targeting; **Microsoft 365 groups** contain only users and work for app assignments, not device policies.
**Dynamic groups** need **Microsoft Entra ID P1** for each unique user in a dynamic user group; devices in dynamic device groups need no licence.
Microsoft recommends **against the Intune Administrator role** for routine work — it's a privileged role; use Intune's own RBAC roles (Policy and Profile Manager, Help Desk Operator…) instead.

**Cloud Device Administrator** can enable, disable and delete devices and read BitLocker keys — and, with Global Administrator, change **device settings** (Intune Administrator only has read-only access there).

**Device settings** control who may register (BYOD) or join devices (**All / Selected / None**), extra local administrators, Microsoft Entra **LAPS**, and the **max devices per user** (default 50, max 100).
For MFA on device registration, prefer a **Conditional Access** policy on the **Register or join devices** user action — and then set the legacy MFA toggle to **No**.
**Administrative units** scope a role to a subset of users, groups or devices (e.g. one region); **PIM** provides time-bound, eligible role assignments (P2).

units.title: Understand the role of Microsoft Entra ID in endpoint management
points: Entra ID handles user authentication, keeps device records and provides groups for policy targeting.

Three device identity types: **registered** (workplace join, BYOD — Windows, macOS, iOS, Android, some Linux), **joined** (corporate Windows 10/11, no on-prem AD needed), **hybrid joined** (on-prem AD–joined plus Entra identity, an interim step).
During enrollment Entra ID authenticates the user and Intune installs an MDM certificate; Conditional Access blocks non-compliant devices until remediated.
Licensing: Entra ID Free (basic), P1 (dynamic groups, hybrid identity), P2 (Identity Protection, PIM), plus an Intune licence for MDM.
Best practice: prefer Entra join over hybrid join for new Windows devices; plan groups before deploying policies; MFA for all admins.

units.title: Create and manage users and groups in Microsoft Entra ID
points: Key user properties: UPN, display name, job title/department, **usage location** (required for licence assignment) and manager.
Bulk operations (CSV create, bulk invite, bulk delete) and **lifecycle workflows** automate onboarding and offboarding.
Membership types: **Assigned** (static), **Dynamic User**, **Dynamic Device**.
Use naming conventions (e.g. `DYN-Devices-Windows11`), nested groups (test inheritance, keep depth shallow) and delegated group owners.
Plan Intune targeting groups by platform, ownership (BYOD vs corporate), department, role and location.

units.title: Assign Microsoft Entra ID roles for device management
points: RBAC = security principal + role definition + scope (directory or administrative unit).

Roles: **Intune Administrator** (full Intune, privileged — setup/emergency only), **Cloud Device Administrator** (enable/disable/delete devices, read BitLocker keys), **Groups Administrator**, **User Administrator**, **Helpdesk Administrator** (password resets for non-admins, read BitLocker keys).
Keep **Global Administrator** to fewer than five people; role assignments can take up to 30 minutes to propagate.
Use PIM eligible (time-bound) assignments for sensitive roles; monitor with audit logs, sign-in logs and access reviews.

units.title: Configure Microsoft Entra ID device registration settings
points: Found under **Identity > Devices > Overview > Device settings**; changes need Cloud Device Administrator or Global Administrator.
The user who joins a device becomes local admin; **additional local administrators** apply to all Entra-joined devices (security groups only). Global Administrators are automatically local admins.
Enabling **Microsoft Entra LAPS** here is step one; you also need a Windows LAPS policy in Intune (**Endpoint security > Account protection**).
Devices enrolled via Autopilot, Apple ADE or Android Enterprise corporate modes are automatically **corporate-owned**; others can be marked by uploading **IMEI or serial number** identifiers.
Deleted devices are soft-deleted for 30 days and still count against the per-user limit; **Enterprise State Roaming** (P1/P2) syncs Windows settings via Entra ID.

units.title: Use dynamic group membership and filters in Microsoft Entra ID
points: A rule = **property + operator + value**, e.g. `user.department -eq "Marketing"` or `device.deviceOSType -eq "Windows"`.
Operators include `-eq`, `-ne`, `-startsWith`, `-contains`, `-in`; combine with `-and`, `-or`, `-not` (precedence: comparison, -not, -and, -or).
Only **security groups** can hold devices; Microsoft 365 groups support dynamic user membership only.
Use **Validate Rules** before saving; updates usually land within 5–10 minutes, initial processing can take hours.
Prefer exact matches over `-contains` (slower), and keep source attributes accurate.

keyTerms.definition: Workplace join for personal (BYOD) devices: device identity, SSO and basic Intune management.
Group whose members are added or removed automatically by a rule on user or device attributes.
Container that limits a role assignment to a subset of users, groups or devices.
Entra role that can enable, disable and delete devices, read BitLocker keys and manage device settings.
Stores and rotates the built-in local admin password of Entra joined and hybrid joined Windows devices.
Uploaded IMEI or serial numbers that mark matching devices as corporate-owned at enrollment.

tables.title: Entra roles for device management
rows: Help desk device actions, device settings
All Microsoft 365 and security groups, naming/expiration policies
Create users and security groups, reset non-admin passwords, licences
Reset non-admin passwords, read BitLocker keys, force sign-out

remember: Device policy targeting → **security group**, not Microsoft 365 group (it can't contain devices).
Dynamic groups → **Entra ID P1 per user** in dynamic user groups; dynamic **device** groups need no licence.
MFA for device registration via Conditional Access → set the legacy device-settings MFA toggle to **No**, or the policy isn't properly enforced.
Intune Administrator can **only read** Entra device settings — change them as Cloud Device Administrator or Global Administrator.

selfCheck.q: Help desk staff must disable lost devices in Entra ID and read BitLocker recovery keys, nothing more. Which role?
selfCheck.a: Cloud Device Administrator.

selfCheck.q: You want only approved users to register personal devices. How do you configure this?
selfCheck.a: Set **Users may register their devices with Microsoft Entra ID** to **Selected** and choose a security group of approved users.

selfCheck.q: Write a rule for a group of all corporate-owned Windows devices.
selfCheck.a: `(device.deviceOSType -eq "Windows") -and (device.deviceOwnership -eq "Company")` in a Dynamic Device security group.

modules.title: Administer device identity and authentication using Microsoft Entra ID
modules.learnSummary: Explore device object lifecycle, join types, trust models, and troubleshooting join and authentication failures in Microsoft Entra ID.
modules.tldr: A device identity is an Entra ID object describing a device (join type, ownership, OS, compliance) that Conditional Access and Intune targeting rely on. Choose registration for BYOD, Entra join for corporate Windows devices and hybrid join only when on-premises AD is still needed. For hybrid Windows Hello for Business, Cloud Kerberos trust is the recommended trust model, and `dsregcmd /status` is your first troubleshooting tool.
objectives: Describe how Microsoft Entra ID represents and manages device identities
Compare device registration, Entra join, and hybrid join scenarios
Explain authentication methods including key trust, certificate trust, and TPM
Configure device trust and join settings using Intune and Microsoft Entra ID
Validate and troubleshoot device identity and trust issues
keyPoints: A **device identity** carries device ID, name, **join type**, **ownership** (Company/Personal), OS version, owners and **compliance/management state**.
**Joining is not managing**: Intune only fully manages a device after **enrollment** — a registered device can still be unmanaged.

**Registration** = BYOD and iOS/Android (device signal for SSO/Conditional Access); **Entra join** = corporate Windows, Entra as primary sign-in; **hybrid join** = on-prem AD plus Entra, needs **Microsoft Entra Connect**.
**Android and iOS** can't be Entra joined or hybrid joined — registration only.
WHfB trust types apply to **hybrid** only: **Cloud Kerberos trust** (recommended, no PKI), **key trust** (PKI for DC certificates), **certificate trust** (PKI for DC and user certificates).
**TPM 2.0** keeps private keys in hardware; Windows 11 requires it, and TPM-backed keys give stronger Conditional Access signals.
Hybrid join requires **Microsoft Entra Connect** (Cloud Sync doesn't support device sync for hybrid join) and devices in a synced OU.
Start troubleshooting with **`dsregcmd /status`** (AzureAdJoined, DomainJoined, TenantId, errors); `dsregcmd /leave` removes the device and breaks Intune and Conditional Access.

units.title: Understand device identities in Microsoft Entra ID
points: Device object attributes drive Conditional Access, Intune targeting, and inventory and reporting.
Lifecycle states: Registered, Entra joined, Hybrid Entra joined (via Microsoft Entra Connect), Managed (enrolled in MDM), Retired/Removed.
Good practice: Entra join for corporate Windows, block personal Windows enrollment, consistent device names/tags, automate retire/wipe.

units.title: Compare device registration, Microsoft Entra join, and hybrid join
points: Registration (workplace join): simple, SSO and Conditional Access for BYOD, but no full management or organizational primary sign-in; main path for iOS/Android Intune management.
Entra join: Entra ID is the primary identity store; supports Autopilot/OOBE provisioning and Windows Hello for Business.
Hybrid join: keeps Group Policy and on-prem resource access plus cloud features, at the cost of Microsoft Entra Connect and extra complexity.
Entra join gives the smoothest sign-in for cloud-first devices.

units.title: Understand authentication methods—key trust, certificate trust, and TPM
points: Cloud-only deployments need **no trust type**.
Cloud Kerberos trust: Entra ID issues a TGT via Microsoft Entra Kerberos; no PKI; shares infrastructure with FIDO2 sign-in.
Key trust: TPM-stored key, on-prem auth needs DC certificates; certificate trust: user certificates too — highest overhead.
All three let users sign in with PIN or biometrics; without a TPM, keys may sit in software keystores (less secure).

units.title: Configure device trust and join settings
points: Entra join + auto-enrollment: in Intune set **Automatic Enrollment** MDM user scope, then sign in during OOBE with **Set up for work or school**.
Hybrid join: configure Microsoft Entra Connect with hybrid join and device writeback, select device OUs, then sync; verify `DomainJoined: YES` and `AzureAdJoined: YES`.
BYOD registration: **Settings > Accounts > Access work or school > Connect**; shows as `Registered` in Entra.
Classic Autopilot needs device registration before OOBE; **Autopilot device preparation** needs no hardware hash pre-registration.

units.title: Validate and troubleshoot device identity and trust issues
points: Checklist: join type in Entra → `dsregcmd /status` → Intune enrollment status → Entra Connect sync health → event logs.
Event log: **Applications and Services Logs > Microsoft > Windows > User Device Registration**.
Devices must reach `login.microsoftonline.com`, `enterpriseregistration.windows.net` and Intune endpoints.
Common fixes: registered-but-unmanaged → check automatic enrollment scope; missing hybrid devices → check Entra Connect OU/device options; WHfB errors → TPM, policy or PKI.

keyTerms.definition: Entra ID object representing one physical or virtual device, used for policy, Conditional Access and Intune targeting.
Another name for Microsoft Entra registration — a lightweight device relationship for BYOD.
Recommended hybrid WHfB model: Entra ID issues Kerberos TGTs via Microsoft Entra Kerberos, no PKI needed.
Trusted Platform Module — hardware that protects private keys from extraction; TPM 2.0 required by Windows 11.
Windows command showing the device's join state, tenant info and last registration errors.

tables.title: Windows Hello for Business trust types (hybrid)
rows: Default for new hybrid deployments and migrations from key trust
PKI already exists for DCs, no user certificates needed
User certificates are a firm requirement

remember: Hybrid WHfB with no PKI → **Cloud Kerberos trust**; cloud-only → **no trust type at all**.
iOS/Android → **registration**, never Entra join or hybrid join.
Device shows Registered but not managed → it was never **enrolled** in Intune; check automatic enrollment scope.
Hybrid devices missing in Entra → **Microsoft Entra Connect** (OU filtering, device options), not Cloud Sync.

selfCheck.q: A hybrid organization without a PKI wants Windows Hello for Business with on-prem access. Which trust type?
selfCheck.a: Cloud Kerberos trust — the only hybrid option with no PKI dependency.

selfCheck.q: Domain-joined PCs don't appear as hybrid joined in Entra ID. What do you check first?
selfCheck.a: Microsoft Entra Connect: device options and hybrid join enabled, the devices' OU is in sync scope, and sync errors.

selfCheck.q: Which command confirms a Windows device is Entra joined, and which value do you look at?
selfCheck.a: `dsregcmd /status` — check that `AzureAdJoined` is YES.

modules.title: Plan and implement device enrollment using Microsoft Intune
modules.learnSummary: Covers enrollment strategy selection, step-by-step platform enrollment guidance for Windows, iOS/iPadOS, macOS, and Android, plus enrollment restrictions and troubleshooting.
modules.tldr: Enrollment strategy starts with ownership: BYOD protects work data while respecting privacy, corporate-owned gives IT full control over the device lifecycle. Each platform has its own methods — Autopilot or automatic enrollment for Windows, ADE for Apple, Android Enterprise for Android — and enrollment restrictions decide which platforms and how many devices may enroll. When enrollment fails, check the Intune management layer and the Entra ID identity layer separately.
objectives: Choose the right enrollment strategy for BYOD and corporate-owned device scenarios
Enroll Windows, iOS/iPadOS, macOS, and Android devices using supported methods
Configure enrollment restrictions to control device type, platform, and device limits
Troubleshoot common device enrollment failures in Microsoft Intune
keyPoints: The device management lifecycle has four phases: **Enroll → Configure → Protect → Retire**; retire can be a reset, full wipe or **selective wipe** of corporate data only.
**BYOD** = manage corporate apps and data, not the OS; **corporate-owned** = IT owns the full lifecycle, from OOBE to wipe.
Windows **automatic enrollment** and **Autopilot** require **Microsoft Entra ID P1/P2**; without P1/P2, use **user-driven** enrollment via **Access work or school**.
**Bulk enrollment** uses a **Windows Configuration Designer** provisioning package; a **Device Enrollment Manager** (DEM) account can enroll up to 1,000 devices.
Apple corporate devices use **ADE** via Apple Business/School Manager; ADE devices are **supervised** by default. For BYOD iOS, **account driven user enrollment** is recommended.

Android Enterprise needs a linked **Managed Google Play** account; modes are **work profile (BYOD)**, **COPE**, **fully managed (COBO)** and **dedicated (COSU)**. Device administrator is **deprecated**.
**Enrollment restrictions** come in two kinds: **device type/platform** (allowed OS, min/max versions, personal devices) and **device limit** (devices per user).
Enrollment fails? Use **Monitor > Enrollment failures** in Intune, check the device's **Enabled** status and device settings in Entra ID, and check **MDM user scope** (MAM scope None).

units.title: Choose an enrollment strategy
points: BYOD: Android work profile, Apple User Enrollment, Company Portal on Windows/macOS; **retire** removes only corporate data.
Corporate single user: Android fully managed, Apple ADE, Windows Autopilot; **wipe** = full factory reset.
COPE balances device-wide control with a separate personal space; kiosk/shared devices use Android dedicated, supervised iOS ADE or Autopilot self-deploying.
Devices without Google Mobile Services use **AOSP**; most organizations need a mix of BYOD and corporate models.

units.title: Enroll Windows devices using Microsoft Intune
points: Requirements: Windows 10 1809+ or Windows 11, internet, Entra user with Intune licence, Entra ID P1/P2 for automatic enrollment, device not joined to another tenant.

Methods: automatic enrollment, Windows Autopilot (user-driven, self-deploying, pre-provision, existing devices), user-driven, bulk (provisioning package or DEM), Configuration Manager co-management (hybrid joined devices).
Choose by ownership, scale and user interaction; never fully manage personal devices without user consent.
Enrolled devices appear under **Devices > All devices**; some inventory can take up to eight hours.

units.title: Enroll iOS and iPadOS devices
points: Corporate methods: Apple Business Manager, ADE (formerly DEP), Apple School Manager, Apple Configurator; ADE needs serial numbers or a purchase order number.

ADE authentication: **Setup Assistant with modern authentication** (recommended — MFA, Entra registration, Conditional Access), Company Portal (device locked until enrolled), legacy Setup Assistant (no MFA).
**Supervised mode** unlocks settings like single-app kiosk mode and silent app installs.
BYOD: Company Portal, web-based enrollment, or **account driven user enrollment** from Settings (recommended, uses JIT registration with Microsoft Authenticator).

units.title: Enroll macOS devices
points: Corporate methods: ABM, ADE, Apple School Manager, Apple Configurator, DEM account; ADE devices can be drop-shipped and enroll in Setup Assistant.
ADE-enrolled Macs are supervised; macOS 11+ needs **User Approved MDM** or ADE for advanced payloads such as kernel extension management.
Tip: configure account settings with **LAPS** (Intune-managed local admin password) plus a standard user account.
BYOD: install the Company Portal `.pkg`, sign in, and approve the management profile in System Settings.

units.title: Enroll Android devices
points: Link Intune to **Managed Google Play** first (Devices > Enrollment > Android).
BYOD: Company Portal from Google Play creates the work profile; IT can't see or wipe personal data.
Fully managed and dedicated devices: factory-reset device, tap the Welcome screen **seven times**, scan the Intune **QR code**; dedicated devices skip user sign-in.
Zero-touch: **Google Zero-Touch** (non-Samsung, authorized reseller, Intune token in DPC extras) and **Samsung Knox Mobile Enrollment**.
Device administrator support ended on GMS devices in August 2024 — migrate to Android Enterprise and block DA with an enrollment restriction.

units.title: Configure enrollment restrictions
points: Restrictions are the gate **before** a device becomes managed and before compliance or Conditional Access apply.
BYOD recommendation: allow common platforms, device limit around 3–5 per user, block unsupported platforms, enforce minimum OS versions.
Corporate recommendation: block personal/unmanaged enrollment types, enforce strict OS requirements, require full enrollment workflows (Autopilot, ADE, Android Enterprise).

units.title: Troubleshoot device enrollment
points: Intune (management layer): last check-in and Sync, compliance tab, **Monitor > Enrollment failures** (restriction or missing licence).
Entra ID (identity layer): a **disabled** device object is blocked even if Intune looks healthy; BitLocker keys, audit logs, and device settings (registration set to None).
"Personal devices are not allowed" on corporate hardware → register via Autopilot/ABM or add **corporate device identifiers**.
Blocked OS → edit the platform restriction's min/max versions; automatic enrollment fails → set **MDM user scope** to All/Some and **MAM user scope** to None.

keyTerms.definition: Apple program (formerly DEP) that enrolls organization-purchased devices over the air during Setup Assistant.
Special account that can enroll up to 1,000 devices for bulk scenarios.
Corporate-owned, personally enabled — corporate device with a separated work profile and personal use allowed.
Google account link required for all Android Enterprise enrollment and app management in Intune.
Intune policy limiting which platforms, OS versions, ownership types and how many devices a user can enroll.
Recommended iOS/iPadOS BYOD method, started from Settings, with work data separated from personal data.

remember: Windows automatic enrollment or Autopilot → requires **Entra ID P1/P2**; no P1/P2 → user-driven enrollment.
Corporate device blocked as "personal" → **corporate device identifiers** or Autopilot/ABM registration, not loosening the restriction.
Android: device administrator is **deprecated** → Android Enterprise; non-GMS devices → **AOSP**.
Overlapping MDM and MAM user scopes during Windows enrollment can cause failures → **MAM scope None**.

selfCheck.q: You must enroll 500 warehouse scanners running Android, locked to one app and with no user sign-in. Which enrollment type?
selfCheck.a: Android Enterprise corporate-owned dedicated devices (COSU), enrolled via QR code or zero-touch.

selfCheck.q: Users get "Personal devices are not allowed" when enrolling new company laptops. What do you do?
selfCheck.a: Register them in Windows Autopilot (or add their serial numbers as corporate device identifiers) so Intune marks them corporate.

selfCheck.q: Which ADE authentication method should you choose to support MFA and Conditional Access during Setup Assistant?
selfCheck.a: Setup Assistant with modern authentication.

modules.title: Deploy Windows devices using Windows Autopilot
modules.learnSummary: Covers Windows Autopilot registration, deployment profiles, pre-provisioning, monitoring, and common troubleshooting scenarios.
modules.tldr: Windows Autopilot provisions new or existing Windows devices from the factory image: the device joins Microsoft Entra ID, enrolls in Intune and receives policies and apps during OOBE — no custom images. You register devices (OEM/partner or hardware hash CSV), assign a deployment profile through an Entra device group, then monitor and troubleshoot deployments in Intune. Pre-provisioning moves the slow device-targeted work to IT, and Autopilot device preparation offers a simpler path for cloud-native Windows 11.
objectives: Describe Windows Autopilot scenarios and deployment benefits
Register and import devices into the Windows Autopilot service
Configure Autopilot deployment profiles and deployment modes
Pre-provision devices using Windows Autopilot
Assign profiles to device groups and monitor Autopilot deployments
Troubleshoot common Windows Autopilot deployment issues
keyPoints: Autopilot **removes custom imaging**: devices ship straight to users, who connect to the internet and sign in; configuration is automatic.

**User-driven** = user signs in and the device is associated with them; **self-deploying** = no user credentials, needs **TPM 2.0 + attestation**, **Entra join only**, only device-targeted compliance applies.
Prefer **Microsoft Entra join** for new devices; hybrid join needs the **Intune Connector for Active Directory** (versions before 6.2501.2000.5 are deprecated — uninstall, then install new).
**Autopilot device preparation**: Windows 11 only, Entra join only, **no hardware hash pre-registration**, uses Enrollment Time Grouping.
Register devices via **OEM/partner**, a CSV from **Get-WindowsAutopilotInfo**, or `-online` import with a **group tag**; Intune needs **automatic MDM enrollment** (MDM user scope).
**Pre-provisioning**: technician presses **Windows key five times** at OOBE, provisions, then **Reseal**; requires TPM 2.0, no VMs.
**Autopilot Reset** removes personal files, apps and settings but keeps the Entra identity and Intune enrollment — not for hybrid joined devices.
Troubleshoot with the **Windows Autopilot deployment status** report (30 days of data), the Provisioning-Diagnostics-Provider event log and `Get-AutopilotDiagnostics`.

units.title: Understand Windows Autopilot scenarios and benefits
points: Scenarios: user-driven, self-deploying, existing devices, pre-provisioned, Autopilot Reset — plus Autopilot device preparation.
User-driven with Entra join needs users allowed to join devices, Autopilot registration, an assigned profile and automatic MDM enrollment.
Self-deploying: near zero-touch, ESP can show progress; Wi-Fi may still need user input for language and network.
Existing devices: reimage (e.g. with Configuration Manager) including an Autopilot configuration file so the next OOBE runs Autopilot.
Device preparation: Windows 11 (24H2, or 23H2/22H2 with KB5035942+), Entra join only; use classic Autopilot for Windows 10, hybrid join, pre-provisioning or existing devices.

units.title: Register and import devices into Autopilot
points: Configure automatic MDM enrollment: **Entra ID > Mobility > Microsoft Intune > MDM user scope** All or Some.
Most common: OEM or partner uploads the hardware info at purchase.
Do-it-yourself: `Install-Script Get-WindowsAutopilotInfo`, export a CSV, then import under **Devices > Windows > Enrollment > Windows Autopilot > Devices > Import**.
`Get-WindowsAutoPilotInfo.ps1 -online -GroupTag "..." -Assign` imports directly with a group tag — handy for testing or onsite builds.

units.title: Configure Autopilot profiles and deployment modes
points: Profile chooses the deployment mode (user-driven or self-deploying) and join type.
**Convert all targeted devices to Autopilot**: registers corporate devices in the targeted groups within about 48 hours (not personal); turning it off doesn't remove entries.
OOBE settings: language, keyboard, EULA, privacy settings, device name and user account type; then assign groups.

units.title: Pre-provision devices using Autopilot
points: Two phases: **technician phase** (device-targeted apps and policies) and **user phase** (user settings and user-targeted policies).
Enable **Allow pre-provisioned deployment** in the profile; at OOBE press Windows key five times → **Windows Autopilot provisioning** → **Provision** → **Reseal**.
No on-prem domain needed during pre-provisioning; for hybrid join, the user phase needs domain controller connectivity.

units.title: Assign profiles and monitor Autopilot deployments
points: Assign profiles to **Entra device groups**; registered devices that join the group get the profile — check **Profile status: Assigned**.
The Windows Autopilot devices list shows serial number, model, assigned user, group tag, enrollment state and profile.
**Devices > Monitor > Windows Autopilot deployment status** shows progress and failures; data kept 30 days.

units.title: Troubleshoot Autopilot deployment issues
points: Check configuration, network connectivity, OOBE behavior (branding), Entra join and MDM enrollment.

Profile settings are stored in `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Provisioning\Diagnostics\Autopilot`; events in **Provisioning-Diagnostics-Provider > Autopilot** (100 = profile not found yet, 171/172 = TPM attestation problems).
**801C0003** = Entra join failed (join permissions or device limit); **80180018** = MDM enrollment failed (licence or too many devices).

keyTerms.definition: Device-specific identifier uploaded (by OEM, partner or CSV) to register a device with Autopilot.
Label on an Autopilot device used to place it in a specific Entra device group.
Screen showing provisioning progress during OOBE while apps and policies install.
Formerly white glove — IT completes the device phase in advance, then reseals the device for the user.
Newer Windows 11, Entra-join-only Autopilot experience using Enrollment Time Grouping, without hash pre-registration.
Returns a device to business-ready state while keeping its Entra identity and Intune enrollment.

tables.title: Autopilot modes at a glance
rows: Hybrid needs Intune Connector for AD

remember: Kiosk or shared device with no user sign-in → **self-deploying** (Entra join only, TPM 2.0 attestation).
Need hybrid join, Windows 10 or pre-provisioning → **classic Autopilot**, not device preparation.
Autopilot Reset keeps **Entra identity and Intune enrollment**, and doesn't work on hybrid joined devices.
801C0003 → **Entra join** problem; 80180018 → **MDM enrollment** problem.

selfCheck.q: A partner should install the large device-targeted apps before laptops ship, so users finish setup quickly. Which feature?
selfCheck.a: Autopilot pre-provisioning — enable Allow pre-provisioned deployment; the technician provisions and reseals the device.

selfCheck.q: Training-room PCs must be returned to a clean, business-ready state after each class without reimaging. What do you use?
selfCheck.a: Windows Autopilot Reset, which keeps the Entra ID identity and Intune enrollment.

selfCheck.q: A user sees error 801C0003 during Autopilot. What do you check?
selfCheck.a: Entra join: whether the user is allowed to join devices and whether they've exceeded the device limit.

paths.title: Manage and maintain devices using Microsoft Intune
paths.summary: Learn how to configure device profiles and compliance policies, manage Windows updates and device lifecycle, monitor device health with analytics and reporting, and troubleshoot device and policy issues using Microsoft Intune.

modules.title: Configure device profiles and policy management using Microsoft Intune
modules.learnSummary: Configure and assign device configuration and compliance policies, and analyze Group Policy migrations using Microsoft Intune.
modules.tldr: Configuration profiles actively push settings to devices; compliance policies only check whether devices meet your rules and report the result to Microsoft Entra ID, where Conditional Access enforces it. Both reach devices through Entra groups, refined with include or exclude assignment filters. Group Policy analytics shows which existing GPO settings can move to Intune, and status reports help you find out why a policy didn't apply.
objectives: Create and configure device configuration profiles for Windows devices
Assign configuration and compliance policies using groups and filters
Create compliance policies and evaluate device compliance
Analyze and migrate Group Policy settings using Group Policy analytics
keyPoints: **Configuration profiles** configure devices proactively; **compliance policies** verify them reactively — and on their own they **don't block access**.

Three ways to build a profile: **templates** (guided, by category), the **settings catalog** (searchable, every supported setting), and **custom profiles** (OMA-URI — only when nothing else has the setting).
Assign **user groups** for user-bound settings (Wi-Fi with credentials, email, VPN) and **device groups** for device settings (encryption, updates).
**Assignment filters** refine a group assignment by device property (ownership, manufacturer, model, OS version/edition, join type) without creating extra groups; **include** filters use AND logic.

Compliance covers **device health** (antivirus, BitLocker/FileVault, secure boot, min OS), **device security** (password, encryption, firewall) and **system security** (TPM, jailbreak/root detection).
**Actions for non-compliance** can escalate over time (email → mark non-compliant → remote lock/wipe); a **grace period** gives users time before enforcement.
**Group Policy analytics** analyzes uploaded GPO backups and labels settings **supported, partially supported or not supported** in Intune.
Policy status values: **Success, Error, Pending, Not applicable, Conflict** — conflicting settings across profiles must be resolved manually.

units.title: Understand device configuration profiles and their role in policy enforcement
points: A profile is a template of settings defined once and assigned to devices or users.

Types: **device profiles** (apply to any user on the device), **user profiles** (follow the user across devices), **administrative templates** (Group Policy–style Windows settings without on-prem infrastructure), **custom profiles** (OMA-URI or Plist).
Multiple profiles layer on one device; conflicting configuration settings surface as a **Conflict** state you resolve manually.

units.title: Create configuration profiles
points: Workflow: choose platform → choose profile type or settings catalog → configure settings → assign → monitor per-device status.
Templates fit standard needs (device restrictions, endpoint protection); settings catalog fits granular, cross-category needs (USB, power, UAC).
Applicability limits a profile by platform and OS version; filters add logic such as "all Windows devices except names starting with TEST".
Several focused profiles assigned to the same group are easier to manage than one large profile.

units.title: Assign configuration profiles using groups and filters
points: All users / all devices fits only mandatory, universal settings.
Dynamic groups add members automatically (e.g. department = Sales, Windows 11 devices) — test rules before assigning critical policies.
Groups carry business logic (region, department); filters carry technical criteria (ownership, model, OS).
**Assigned ≠ applicable**: a profile isn't applied if a filter excludes the device or the platform doesn't match.

units.title: Create compliance policies
points: Created per platform; results are compliant, non-compliant or not evaluated.
A device is compliant only if it meets **all** enabled requirements.
Intune reports compliance to Entra ID; **Conditional Access** requires a compliant device for apps like Teams, SharePoint or Exchange Online.
The compliance dashboard shows the overall rate and why devices fail (e.g. missing BitLocker).

units.title: Assign compliance policies using groups and filters
points: User group assignment evaluates every device of users in the group; device group assignment applies regardless of who signs in.
Evaluation order: in group? → matches all include filters? → matches an exclude filter? → apply and evaluate.
Example: assign to all corporate Windows devices and add an exclude filter for the Surface Go model.
Keep filter logic simple, pilot first, document and review assignments periodically.

units.title: Analyze and migrate Group Policy using Group Policy analytics
points: Export GPO backups with the **Group Policy Management Console**, upload them in the Intune admin center, and review the report.
Supported settings are quick wins; partially supported ones need a judgment call; unsupported ones need custom OMA-URI, an alternative, or a conscious decision to drop them.
Migrate in phases (critical security settings first) instead of an all-at-once cutover.

units.title: Troubleshoot device configuration and policy application issues
points: Drill down from policy overview → device/user status → per-setting status; or from **Devices > All devices** > device > Configuration/Compliance.
The **Troubleshooting + Support** blade shows a user's enrollment, compliance, assignments and sync history in one place.
Common causes: wrong group, filter excluding the device, not enrolled/compliant, licensing, sync delays, conflicting settings.
Workflow: verify assignment → check eligibility → review reports → manual sync → troubleshooting tool → check conflicts → fix root cause.

keyTerms.definition: Searchable list of all Intune-supported settings for building granular profiles.
Profile that deploys a setting by its raw OMA-URI path when no template or catalog setting exists.
Include or exclude rule on device properties applied at assignment time to refine a group target.
Set of requirements Intune evaluates on a device; the result feeds Conditional Access.
Time a non-compliant device gets before it's marked non-compliant and actions are enforced.
Intune tool that analyzes GPO backups and shows which settings can migrate to Intune.

tables.title: Profile creation approaches
rows: Must know which settings you need
Settings missing from templates and catalog
Requires exact syntax and expertise; more risk

remember: Compliance policy alone **doesn't block** anything → you need **Conditional Access** requiring a compliant device.
Exclude a few models from a broad assignment → **exclude filter**, not a new group.
Custom OMA-URI profile → **last resort**, only when the setting isn't in a template or the settings catalog.
Status **Pending** → device hasn't checked in yet (sync); **Not applicable** → wrong platform; **Conflict** → two policies set the same setting differently.

selfCheck.q: You want to move hundreds of on-premises GPO settings to Intune and need to know which have equivalents. What do you use?
selfCheck.a: Group Policy analytics — upload GPO backups exported from the Group Policy Management Console and review supported/partial/unsupported settings.

selfCheck.q: A strict compliance policy should apply to all corporate Windows devices except Surface Go. How?
selfCheck.a: Assign it to the corporate device group and add an exclude filter on the Surface Go model.

selfCheck.q: A profile shows Conflict on several devices. What's the cause and fix?
selfCheck.a: Another policy configures the same setting with a different value; edit one policy or reassign them so the setting is defined once.

modules.title: Monitor and maintain devices using Microsoft Intune
modules.learnSummary: Use Endpoint Analytics, proactive remediation, reporting, and automation to monitor and maintain device health and compliance.
modules.tldr: Monitoring tells you whether the right settings reach the right devices: policy status reports, device records and sync cycles come first. Endpoint analytics scores startup performance, app reliability and remote-work readiness, while Remediations detect and fix common Windows issues with script packages. Update ring and feature update reports, compliance reports and PowerShell with Microsoft Graph complete the maintenance toolkit.
objectives: Use Endpoint Analytics to assess device health and performance
Implement Remediations to fix common device issues
Monitor Windows Update rings and feature update deployments
Generate and interpret device and compliance reports
keyPoints: Policy status values: **Succeeded, Error, Conflict, Pending, Not applicable**; use **Per setting status** and the **Configuration policy assignment failures** report to pinpoint problems.
Devices check in about every **8 hours**; newly enrolled Windows devices check in every 3 minutes for 15 minutes, then every 15 minutes for 2 hours. **Sync** forces an immediate check-in.
The **Endpoint analytics score** (0–100) is a weighted average of **startup performance**, **application reliability** and **work from anywhere**.
**Advanced Analytics** (resource performance, battery health, anomalies, device timeline, device query) requires **Intune Suite** or the Advanced Analytics add-on.
A **Remediations** package = detection script + optional remediation script; remediation runs only when detection returns **exit 1**.
Remediations need Entra joined or hybrid joined Windows Enterprise/Pro/Education devices (or co-managed) and an eligible **Windows E3/E5, A3/A5 or VDA** licence.
**Update rings** decide *how and when* updates install; **feature update policies** decide *which Windows version* is offered — never a downgrade.
Use **Microsoft Graph PowerShell** (`Connect-MgGraph` with least-privilege scopes) to automate reporting and bulk tasks.

units.title: Understand the role of monitoring in endpoint management
points: Profiles are listed under **Devices > Manage devices > Configuration**; open one for **Device and user check-in status**, **Device assignment status** and **Per setting status**.
Find conflicts per device: **All devices** > device > **Device configuration** > setting in Conflict shows the policies involved.
After deployment Intune notifies the device (usually under five minutes) and retries three more times; offline devices get the policy at the next scheduled check-in.
Users can also sync from the Company Portal app.

units.title: Use Endpoint Analytics to monitor device health and performance
points: Enable via **Reports > Endpoint analytics**; a guided setup creates the **Intune data collection policy**.
**Model scores** and **Device scores** tabs spot underperforming hardware and individual devices; compare against baselines to catch regressions.
Startup performance: boot + sign-in score, 29 days of events. Application reliability: crashes/hangs over 14 days.
Work from anywhere covers Windows, cloud management, cloud identity and cloud provisioning.

units.title: Use Remediations to fix common device issues
points: Found under **Devices > Manage devices > Scripts and remediations**; built-in packages (e.g. update stale Group Policies) or up to 200 custom packages.
Scripts: UTF-8 (no BOM if signature check is enforced), output max 2,048 characters, no reboot commands, passwords or personal data.
Run by the **Intune Management Extension** on a schedule — once, hourly or daily; missed runs execute when the device is back online.
Monitor Detected/Remediated/Failed per package, export to CSV, and use **Run remediation (preview)** for an on-demand run on one device.

units.title: Monitor Windows Update rings and feature update deployments
points: Policy types: Windows Update client policy, update ring, feature update, quality update (expedite, hotpatch), driver update.
Typical rollout: one feature update policy for all devices plus rings for test (0 days), pilot (10 days) and production (30 days) deferral.
When several feature policies apply, only the **latest** applicable version is offered; an **optional** feature update requires Windows Autopatch licensing.
Feature update reports show Pending, Offering, Downloading, Installing, Restart Required and Installed.

units.title: View device and policy health in the Intune admin center
points: Check **last check-in time** first — without recent check-in, status data can be stale.
The device record shows hardware details, discovered apps (7-day refresh cycle), device compliance, device configuration, app configuration and managed apps.

units.title: Generate and interpret device and compliance reports
points: No dedicated inventory report: use **All devices** with columns, filters and **Export** (zipped CSV).
**Reports > Device compliance**: Summary tab, the device compliance report (large datasets, filters on status, OS, ownership), and **compliance trends** over time.

units.title: Automate management tasks using PowerShell
points: Microsoft Graph gives programmatic access to all Intune data and operations.
Access uses delegated or application permissions defined in an Entra app registration — choose only the scopes you need.
`Install-Module Microsoft.Graph`, then `Connect-MgGraph -Scopes "DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All"` for read-only reporting.

keyTerms.definition: Intune reports that turn device telemetry into scores for startup, app reliability and work-from-anywhere readiness.
Detection and remediation PowerShell script packages that find and fix common Windows issues on a schedule.
Windows agent that downloads and runs Intune scripts such as Remediations.
Policy controlling deferrals, deadlines, restarts and user experience for Windows updates.
Policy that pins which Windows version is offered to a device.
Device contact with Intune when it receives policies and reports status; roughly every 8 hours.

tables.title: Device check-in frequency
rows: Every 3 min for 15 min, then every 15 min for 2 hours

remember: Remediation script runs **only on exit 1** from detection — exit 0 means no issue, no action.
Update ring = **how/when**; feature update policy = **which version**.
Resource performance, battery health, anomalies, device query → **Advanced Analytics** (Intune Suite/add-on), not basic Endpoint analytics.
Status **Pending** → check **last check-in** and force a **Sync** before deeper troubleshooting.

selfCheck.q: Users complain that laptops boot slowly. Where do you look to find the affected devices and models?
selfCheck.a: Endpoint analytics — the Startup performance report plus the Model scores and Device scores tabs.

selfCheck.q: You want to automatically restart a service that keeps stopping on Windows devices. What do you deploy?
selfCheck.a: A Remediations script package: a detection script that exits 1 when the service is stopped and a remediation script that restarts it.

selfCheck.q: A device is on Windows 11 24H2 and receives a feature update policy for 23H2. What happens?
selfCheck.a: Nothing — feature update policies don't downgrade devices.

modules.title: Manage Windows updates and lifecycle using Microsoft Intune
modules.learnSummary: Configure update rings, feature updates, Hotpatch, and Autopatch to manage Windows servicing and lifecycle using Intune.
modules.tldr: Windows gets monthly quality updates and periodic feature updates, delivered through a servicing channel (Current Channel or Enterprise LTSC) within a support window. In Intune you stage updates with update rings (deferrals, deadlines, restarts), pin versions with feature update policies, skip restarts with Hotpatch, or hand the whole process to Windows Autopatch. The module ends with troubleshooting failed updates and with retiring, wiping or resetting devices at end of life.
objectives: Explain Windows servicing channels and update types
Implement update rings and feature update deployments in Intune
Configure Hotpatch and use Windows Autopatch for automated update management
Troubleshoot update deployment and compliance issues
keyPoints: Update types: **quality** (monthly security/reliability fixes, small, low risk), **feature** (new capabilities, larger, need testing), **preview** (optional, test before mandatory).
**Current Channel** = frequent feature releases for fast adopters; **Enterprise LTSC** = feature updates every 2–3 years, monthly security only — for medical, industrial and kiosk devices.
**Update rings** stage rollouts (e.g. pilot 0 days → standard 30 → conservative 90) with deferrals, pause, active hours and deadlines; **don't assign a device to more than one ring**.
**Feature update policy** = which version; **update ring** = when and how. The ring's schedule controls when the feature update takes effect.
**Hotpatch** applies security fixes in memory with **no restart**: Windows 11 24H2+, eligible licence, latest quarterly baseline, **VBS on**, enabled in a **Windows quality update policy**.
**Windows Autopatch** automates Windows and Microsoft 365 Apps updates through **Test, First, Second and Broad** rings and pauses problematic updates automatically.
Moving between General Availability and Insider Preview is a policy change; moving **to or from LTSC requires a reinstall/edition change**.
Troubleshoot with the update ring and compliance reports, `Get-WindowsUpdateLog`, **CBS.log**, **SetupDiag** and DISM logs; **pausing** a ring stops new deployments but doesn't uninstall.

units.title: Understand the Windows servicing model and update types
points: Channels: Current Channel, Enterprise LTSC; the Semi-Annual Channel is deprecated in favor of deferral policies.
Each version has a **servicing window**; deferring only postpones within it — after it closes, devices must upgrade to stay supported.
Tiered deployment: security updates to a test group, validate 1–2 weeks, then organization-wide; feature updates need longer testing.

units.title: Implement update rings and feature update policies in Intune
points: Ring settings: feature and quality update deferral (days), pause feature/quality updates, automatic update behavior, active hours, deadline.
Quality update deferral is usually 0 so security updates deploy immediately.
Overlapping rings or Settings Catalog update settings cause a **conflict** — use Autopatch groups or assignment filters for predictable staging.
The update rings report shows devices per ring, compliance, awaiting restart and failures.

units.title: Configure and manage Hotpatch with Microsoft Intune
points: Licences: Windows 11 Enterprise E3/E5, Microsoft 365 F3, Windows 11 Education A3/A5, Microsoft 365 Business Premium or Windows 365 Enterprise; Arm64 needs CHPE disabled.
Enable: **Quality updates** tab > Windows quality update policy > "apply without restarting the device (Hotpatch)" = **Allow**; existing rings stay as they are.
Ineligible devices fall back to the standard LCU with a restart — frequent fallbacks may point to VBS or Secure Boot issues.
Not every fix can be hotpatched; plan for restart-required updates too.

units.title: Manage Windows servicing channels for enterprise devices
points: Standard business devices → Current Channel with rings; specialized devices → LTSC; Preview Channel (Windows Insider) only on a few validation devices.
Set channels through Autopilot profiles, Settings Catalog (`Update/BranchReadinessLevel`, `Update/ManagePreviewBuilds`) or feature update policies.
Current Channel needs capacity to validate each release within about 60–90 days; start LTSC migration testing 12 months before support ends.

units.title: Implement Windows Autopatch for automated update management
points: Default rings: **Test** (1–2 business days), **First** (7 days), **Second** (14 days), **Broad** (28 days).
Devices: Pro, Enterprise or Education, enrolled in Intune with **device-based** enrollment, Microsoft 365 Apps installed.
Enable under **Tenant administration > Windows Autopatch**; pilot on IT devices for 4–6 weeks; aim for at least 95% success.
A device can't be in an Autopatch ring and a separate update ring for the same update type — pick one approach per device.

units.title: Troubleshoot update deployment and compliance issues
points: Common causes: low disk space (about 10–15 GB needed for feature updates), connectivity drops, app or driver incompatibility, BIOS/firmware.
Same error code on many devices → systematic issue; failures clustered in one ring → look for shared model, app or network segment.
Quality gates: review pilot results before promotion, pause rings if failures exceed a threshold, test apps and inventory drivers.

units.title: Retire and reset devices using Microsoft Intune
points: **Retire** removes the device from Intune management; it shows as retired in reports for 90 days, then is deleted.
Windows **Wipe** by default is a factory reset; options: **keep enrollment state and user account** (stays enrolled) or **continue to wipe even if the device loses power** (lost/stolen).
For stolen devices, wipe — don't rely on retire alone; after wipe the device usually re-enrolls via Autopilot.
Bulk actions from **All devices**; keep disposal records (device ID, serial, owner, action, date) for compliance audits.

keyTerms.definition: Period Microsoft supports a Windows version; devices must move to a newer version before it closes.
Long-Term Servicing Channel: feature updates every 2–3 years, monthly security updates, Enterprise LTSC edition only.
Intune policy setting deferrals, pauses, deadlines and restart behavior for a group of devices.
Security updates applied in memory to the running kernel without a restart, on eligible Windows 11 24H2+ devices.
Cloud service that automates Windows and Microsoft 365 Apps updates through staged rings with health monitoring.
Microsoft tool that analyzes failed Windows feature update setups.

tables.title: Windows Autopatch default rings
rows: Small pilot group validates compatibility first
Larger group after First ring is stable

tables.title: Servicing channels
rows: A few validation devices, not production

remember: Security fix without a restart → **Hotpatch** (quality update policy, VBS on, Windows 11 24H2+), not an update ring setting.
Switch to or from **LTSC** → reinstall/edition change, not just an Intune policy.
Pausing an update ring **doesn't uninstall** updates that are already applied.
Device in **two update rings** (or ring + Autopatch for the same update type) → conflict; one approach per device.

selfCheck.q: A trading floor can't tolerate restarts but needs security fixes quickly. Which feature and requirements apply?
selfCheck.a: Hotpatch — eligible licence, Windows 11 24H2+, latest baseline, VBS enabled, and a Windows quality update policy with Hotpatch set to Allow.

selfCheck.q: A feature update breaks a business app after the pilot ring installed it. What do you do immediately?
selfCheck.a: Pause feature updates on the affected rings; it stops new deployments but doesn't remove the update where it's already installed.

selfCheck.q: A laptop with company data is stolen. Retire or wipe?
selfCheck.a: Wipe (optionally continuing even if the device loses power); retire alone isn't enough for stolen devices.

modules.title: Troubleshoot device and policy issues using Microsoft Intune
modules.learnSummary: Investigate and resolve device enrollment, configuration, and policy application issues using Intune diagnostics and remediation techniques.
modules.tldr: Intune troubleshooting follows a fixed workflow: scope the problem, check service health, use the Troubleshooting blade, inspect policy and app status, analyze client logs, then remediate or escalate. Enrollment failures usually come from licensing, MDM scope or enrollment restrictions; compliance failures from one failing setting or a stale sync; and policy conflicts are resolved with exclusion groups. Remediation scripts automate recurring fixes before users notice.
objectives: Describe the Intune troubleshooting workflow and common failure modes
Troubleshoot enrollment, compliance, and profile conflicts
Use logs, diagnostics, and the Intune Troubleshooting blade for user/device investigations
Automate remediation with scripts and remediation tools
keyPoints: Six phases: **scope → service health (Tenant status) → Troubleshooting portal → policy/app status → client-side logs → remediate or escalate**.
Scope first: everyone affected → likely a **service issue or global policy**; one user → **local device state or group membership**.
Most blocked enrollments come from **enrollment restrictions** (platform, ownership, device limit); also check **Intune licence** and **MDM user scope**.
**Not evaluated** ≠ non-compliant: the device hasn't processed the policy yet. Devices with **no compliance policy count as Compliant** by default.
Precedence: config vs config → **Conflict** (neither applied); **compliance beats configuration**; standard UI usually beats custom OMA-URI; Endpoint security vs config → Conflict.
**App protection policies** don't conflict — the **most restrictive** setting wins.
**Collect diagnostics** pulls a log bundle remotely; read **MDMDiagReport.html** and the **DeviceManagement-Enterprise-Diagnostics-Provider** log (event 404 = failure, 814 = applied).
**Remediations** (detection exits 1 → remediation runs) automate Tier 1 fixes; track the **Issue fixed** count to show tickets prevented.

units.title: Understand the troubleshooting workflow in Microsoft Intune
points: Gather the exact UPN and device, expected vs actual behavior, and scope.
Check **Tenant administration > Tenant status** for incidents before local troubleshooting.
Client side: Windows sync via Access work or school, **Collect diagnostics**, Event Viewer; mobile: Company Portal **Send logs**.
Escalate via **Help and support** with UPN, device ID and error codes.
With Copilot: device comparison prompts; Security Copilot agents (Change Review, Device Offboarding, Policy Configuration, Vulnerability Remediation) need a Security Copilot licence.

units.title: Troubleshoot device enrollment and compliance failures
points: Enrollment symptoms: unsupported Windows version, personal devices not allowed, device limit reached, device never appears.
Check licence, **Automatic Enrollment** MDM user scope, platform and device limit restrictions, and Autopilot/ADE profile assignment.
Compliance: open the device's **Device compliance** tab to find the failing setting, force a sync, verify the assignment.
Use grace periods and noncompliance emails; if Intune says Compliant but access is blocked, check **Entra sign-in logs** for another Conditional Access condition.

units.title: Troubleshoot configuration profile and policy conflicts
points: Spot conflicts at profile level (Device status), device level (Device configuration) and per setting.
Manage security settings only from the **Endpoint security** node to avoid conflicts with configuration profiles.
Best fix: **exclusion groups** — e.g. exclude Marketing Devices from an All Devices baseline that disables the camera.
Frequent conflicts → consolidate into fewer profiles, preferably Settings Catalog.

units.title: Use logs and diagnostics to investigate device issues
points: Remote: **Collect diagnostics**, then download from **Monitor > Device diagnostics** (registry keys, MDM event logs, system info).
Local: **Access work or school > Info > Create report** → `C:\Users\Public\Documents\MDMDiagnostics\MDMDiagReport.html`.
Mobile: Company Portal **Send logs** returns an **Incident ID** for Microsoft Support.
Event IDs: **814** policy applied, **404** failure (shows the CSP/registry path), **11** sync session start; Endpoint analytics gives proactive telemetry.

units.title: Use the Intune Troubleshooting blade for user-based diagnostics
points: **Troubleshooting + support > Troubleshoot > Select user** gives one user-centric view.
Check user status, Intune licence and group memberships, then the **Devices** tab for compliance per device.
Example: iPad blocked from email → compliance setting "minimum OS version iOS 16.0" failed on iOS 15.4 → user updates iOS and syncs.

units.title: Automate issue resolution using remediation scripts
points: Built-in packages: **Update stale Group Policies**, **Restart Office Click-to-run service**.
Use cases: restart stopped services, clear stale caches, re-enforce registry keys, fix shortcuts.
Logged-on credentials **No** = runs as SYSTEM (services, HKLM); **Yes** for HKCU or user data.
Device status states: **Without issues**, **Issue fixed**, **Failed**; **Run remediation (preview)** runs a package on one device immediately.

keyTerms.definition: Troubleshooting + support > Troubleshoot: one view of a user's licence, groups, devices, compliance and enrollment failures.
State when two configuration policies set the same setting differently; Intune applies neither until resolved.
Compliance state meaning the device hasn't processed the policy yet — not the same as non-compliant.
Remote action that zips a Windows device's registry keys, MDM event logs and system info for download.
Readable summary of applied policies, enrollment details and configuration state on a Windows device.
Formerly Proactive remediations — detection and remediation PowerShell scripts run on a schedule.

tables.title: Who wins when policies overlap?
rows: Custom OMA-URI vs standard UI setting
App protection policy vs app protection policy

remember: Everyone affected → check **Tenant status** first, not individual devices.
Intune shows Compliant but user still blocked → **Entra sign-in logs** (other Conditional Access conditions).
Two app protection policies with different PINs → **most restrictive** wins; two configuration profiles → **Conflict**.
Fix a conflict with an **exclusion group** on the broad policy, not by deleting the baseline.

selfCheck.q: A user's iPad is blocked from email right after enrollment. What's the fastest way to find the reason?
selfCheck.a: Open the Troubleshooting blade for the user, select the iPad in the Devices tab and review the Device Compliance tab to find the failing setting.

selfCheck.q: A compliance policy requires a 14-character password and a configuration profile sets 8. Which applies?
selfCheck.a: The compliance policy — compliance always wins over configuration.

selfCheck.q: A Windows device's custom OMA-URI setting won't apply. Where do you find the failing CSP path?
selfCheck.a: In Event Viewer under DeviceManagement-Enterprise-Diagnostics-Provider > Admin — event ID 404 shows the failure, locally or via Collect diagnostics.
