modules.tldr: Microsoft Cloud PKI is a cloud-hosted certificate authority inside Intune, so you no longer need on-premises NDES servers or certificate connectors. You build a root CA and issuing CA, deploy trusted certificate profiles, then SCEP profiles that let devices enroll and renew certificates automatically. Reports, audit logs and the CRL keep certificate health under control.
objectives: Describe how Microsoft Cloud PKI replaces on-premises certificate infrastructure
Create a root CA and issuing CA hierarchy in the Microsoft Intune admin center
Deploy trusted certificate profiles and SCEP certificate profiles in the correct order
Configure validity periods, renewal thresholds, key usage, and EKUs for SCEP profiles
Monitor certificate health, audit administrative actions, and remediate common issuance and renewal problems
keyPoints: Cloud PKI needs the **Intune Suite** or the **Cloud PKI standalone add-on**; CAs created during a **trial** stay **software-backed** and can't be converted to HSM-backed keys.
Maximum **six CAs per tenant**, counting root, issuing and BYOCA together.
Two-tier hierarchy: **root CA** (trust anchor, e.g. 25 years, RSA-4096/SHA-512) and **issuing CA** (e.g. 5 years) with a **built-in SCEP service** and SCEP URI.
Deployment order: **root CA → issuing CA → trusted cert profile (root) → trusted cert profile (issuing) → SCEP profile**; SCEP before trust means rejected certificates.
**BYOCA** creates an Intune issuing CA that chains to your existing on-prem or third-party root.
The **private key is generated on the device and never leaves it**; the SCEP challenge proves the request comes from a managed device.
**Renewal threshold** defaults to **20%** of lifetime remaining; renewal only works for devices that check in.
CRL: valid **7 days**, refreshed every **3.5 days**, updated **immediately** on manual revocation; retire or wipe revokes a device's certificates automatically.

units.title: Set up cloud-based PKI
points: RBAC permissions (managed in Intune roles): Read CAs, Create CAs, Revoke issued leaf certificates, Disable and reenable CAs; Intune Administrator includes them.
Create CAs in Tenant administration > Cloud PKI; CA keys are generated in Azure Managed HSM (licensed tenants).
Trust is deployed with two **Trusted certificate** profiles (root and issuing CA certificates downloaded from the CA page).
SCEP profile: device or user certificate, validity, KSP (software or TPM), key usage, root certificate = issuing CA trust profile, SCEP Server URL = issuing CA's SCEP URI.
One SCEP profile per platform (Windows, iOS/iPadOS, Android, macOS).

units.title: Automate certificate issuance and renewal
points: Subject and SAN use variables such as `CN={{DeviceId}}`, `CN={{UserPrincipalName}}`; include the UPN as SAN for Wi-Fi/VPN.
Validity: 1 year common, 90 days more secure; at 20% threshold a one-year cert renews about 73 days before expiry, and the old cert is revoked.
Match the EKU to the purpose: client authentication (1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2), secure email (…3.4), code signing (…3.3); mismatched EKUs fail authentication.
Windows KSP: TPM if present otherwise software, or TPM otherwise fail to enforce hardware-backed keys.
Verify in Devices > Monitor > Certificates, with `certutil -store My`, or in Event Viewer under CertificateServicesClient.

units.title: Monitor certificate health and compliance
points: View all certificates per issuing CA (updated every 24 hours, first 1,000 only); Devices > Monitor > Certificates shows the full list.
States: Active, Expired (often offline past the renewal window), Revoked (manual or via wipe/retire/unenrollment).
Audit logs: Tenant administration > Audit logs, category Cloud PKI; export to a SIEM for long-term retention.
Applications may cache the CRL, so pair revocation with Conditional Access for immediate blocking.
No built-in expiry alerts: export reports, route Entra sign-in logs to Log Analytics, or use compliance + Conditional Access.

keyTerms.definition: Top of the hierarchy and trust anchor that devices are configured to trust.
CA under the root that signs device and user certificates and hosts the built-in SCEP service.
Simple Certificate Enrollment Protocol — automates certificate enrollment for large numbers of devices.
Bring Your Own CA — an Intune issuing CA chained to an existing external root CA.
Percentage of certificate lifetime remaining when automatic renewal starts (default 20%).
Extended key usage — defines what a certificate may be used for, such as client authentication.
Certificate Revocation List checked by relying parties to confirm a certificate isn't revoked.

tables.title: Troubleshooting Cloud PKI
rows: Trust and SCEP profiles assigned to the same group, trust profiles arrive first (no blocking filters), device enrolled and can reach the SCEP URI
Device not checking in during renewal window; start renewal earlier (e.g. 30–40% threshold) or use shorter validity for remote devices
Both trust profiles on the device, EKU and subject/SAN match what the authentication server expects

remember: Want certificates without NDES or the certificate connector → **Cloud PKI** (built-in SCEP per issuing CA).
Devices reject issued certificates → **trusted certificate profiles must deploy before SCEP**.
Wi-Fi rejects an email-signing certificate → **EKU mismatch**; use client authentication.
Need a lost device blocked right now → revoke **and** use **Conditional Access**, because apps may cache the CRL.

selfCheck.q: You run a Cloud PKI trial and plan to keep the CAs after purchasing. What limitation applies?
selfCheck.a: Trial CAs use software-backed keys and can't be converted to HSM-backed keys later.

selfCheck.q: Your company has an existing on-premises root CA it wants to keep as trust anchor. Which Cloud PKI option fits?
selfCheck.a: Bring Your Own CA (BYOCA), creating an Intune issuing CA that chains to the existing root.

selfCheck.q: Windows devices must store certificate keys in hardware or not enroll at all. Which KSP setting?
selfCheck.a: Enroll to Trusted Platform Module (TPM) KSP, otherwise fail.

paths.title: Automate and optimize endpoint management using Microsoft Intune
paths.summary: Learn how to automate endpoint management with PowerShell and Microsoft Graph, optimize device management using AI and Copilot, and monitor and optimize endpoint performance using Microsoft Intune.

modules.title: Automate endpoint management using PowerShell and Microsoft Graph
modules.learnSummary: Automate Microsoft Intune operations at scale using PowerShell and the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK, including device management, policy assignment, and secure authentication.
modules.tldr: Microsoft Graph is the main API for automating Intune, called directly over REST, through the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK or from other SDKs. Unattended automation uses a Microsoft Entra app registration with least-privilege **application permissions**, admin consent and a certificate, federated credential or managed identity. Intune can also run PowerShell scripts on Windows devices through the Intune Management Extension.
objectives: Use Microsoft Graph and the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK to script common Intune tasks.
Query device inventory, filter devices, and update device properties programmatically.
Integrate Microsoft Defender and mobile threat defense signals into automation workflows.
Register Microsoft Entra ID applications and apply least-privilege Graph permissions.
Build repeatable scripts and runbooks for scheduled and event-driven automation.
keyPoints: Four approaches: **PowerShell scripting**, **Graph API/SDKs**, **event-driven** (Logic Apps, Power Automate, Azure Functions on Graph change notifications) and **managed runbooks** (Azure Automation).

Prefer the **Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK** (v2.x) over older Intune-specific modules; every cmdlet calls a Graph endpoint (e.g. `Get-MgDeviceManagementManagedDevice` → `deviceManagement/managedDevices`).
**App-only access** (application permissions, no user) for unattended jobs; **delegated access** for interactive troubleshooting.
Register the app in **Entra admin center > App registrations**, add only the needed `DeviceManagement*` application permissions and **Grant admin consent**.

Credentials: **certificates** for production, client secrets only for development (short expiry, Key Vault), **federated credentials** for pipelines, **managed identity** for Azure Automation/Functions.
Intune **PowerShell scripts** run via the IME: once by default, up to 3 retries, 30-minute timeout, under 200 KB, checked hourly.
**Settings Catalog** policies live under `deviceManagement/configurationPolicies`; `deviceConfigurations` is only for legacy template profiles.

units.title: Understand automation options for managing Microsoft Intune
points: PowerShell for one-off fixes and scheduled maintenance; Graph SDKs for production integrations; Power Automate/Logic Apps for low-code workflows; runbooks for orchestration, retries and scheduling.
Event-driven flow: Intune event → Graph change notification → Azure Function/Logic App → remediation or ITSM ticket.
Event-driven automation requires managing webhook subscriptions, securing receiving endpoints and handling retries.
Device Query (KQL, near real time) is part of Advanced Analytics, which needs licensing on top of Intune Plan 1 (included in Microsoft 365 E3 from July 2026).
Governance: dedicated app registrations, secrets in Key Vault or managed identities, logging and alerting.

units.title: Register and secure Microsoft Graph API access for Intune
points: New registration: single tenant for one organization, no redirect URI for server-to-server; note the client ID and tenant ID.
Read-only device query needs only `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All`; add Configuration, Apps or ServiceConfig permissions only if needed.
API permissions > Add a permission > Microsoft Graph > Application permissions > Grant admin consent.
Verify the app can get a token for `https://graph.microsoft.com/.default`.

units.title: Authenticate and use the Microsoft Graph API for Intune
points: Use REST directly for HTTP-level control or non-PowerShell services; the SDK for objects, pipelines and simpler auth.
`Install-Module Microsoft.Graph` (or `Microsoft.Graph.DeviceManagement`); SDK v1.x and v2.x aren't fully backward-compatible.
`Connect-MgGraph` with `-CertificateThumbprint` or `-ClientSecretCredential` for app-only; `-Scopes` for delegated sign-in.
Test with `Get-MgDeviceManagementManagedDevice`, `Get-MgDeviceManagementDeviceConfiguration`, `Get-MgDeviceManagementMobileApp`.
*Insufficient privileges/Forbidden* → check application permissions, admin consent, tenant and client IDs.

units.title: Use PowerShell to run scripts against Microsoft Intune
points: Requirements: Windows 10 1607+, Entra joined or hybrid joined, Intune-enrolled, script under 200 KB.
**Devices > Scripts and remediations > Add > Windows 10 and later**: upload .ps1, choose User or System context, optional signature check and 64-bit host.
Runs once; reruns only if the content or assignment changes; scripts generally run before Win32 app installs.
Make scripts idempotent and keep secrets out of them.

units.title: Automate device and policy tasks using Microsoft Graph
points: POST to `deviceCompliancePolicies` to create a policy (e.g. require BitLocker), then POST `/{policyId}/assign` with a group ID.
Settings Catalog: GET, PATCH and assign via `configurationPolicies`.
Change assignments without recreating policies, e.g. move from pilot to broad audience.
Find non-compliant devices with `managedDevices?$filter=complianceState ne 'compliant'`.
Common permissions: `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read(Write).All`, `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read(Write).All`.

keyTerms.definition: Primary REST API for Intune devices, configuration, apps and compliance.
PowerShell wrapper around Graph that handles authentication, paging and object output.
Authentication where the registered app uses application permissions without a signed-in user.
Tenant-wide approval required before an app can use its application permissions.
Webhook that triggers automation when something changes, such as compliance state.
Azure-managed identity for services like Azure Automation or Functions, so no stored credentials are needed.

tables.title: Which automation approach?
rows: One-off fixes or scheduled admin tasks
Power Automate or Logic Apps with Graph connectors
Azure Automation runbooks or an orchestration platform
Graph change notifications → Azure Function/Logic App

remember: Unattended script → **application** permissions + admin consent, not delegated.
Production credential → **certificate** (or managed identity), not a client secret.
New Settings Catalog policy via Graph → **configurationPolicies**, not deviceConfigurations.
Intune PowerShell script doesn't run again → it only reruns when **content or assignment changes**.

selfCheck.q: A nightly runbook must read Intune device inventory. Which permission model and minimum permission?
selfCheck.a: App-only access with the DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All application permission and admin consent.

selfCheck.q: Your script calling Graph returns Forbidden. What do you check?
selfCheck.a: That the right DeviceManagement application permissions were added, admin consent was granted, and the correct tenant and client IDs are used.

selfCheck.q: A remediation script must change machine-wide registry settings. Which run context?
selfCheck.a: System context, which runs with local system privileges.

modules.title: Optimize device management using AI and Copilot tools
modules.learnSummary: Use AI and Copilot tools across Microsoft Intune and Microsoft Defender to prioritize endpoint issues, investigate threats, and apply targeted remediation actions.
modules.tldr: AI turns endpoint telemetry into recommendations, prioritization and predictable remediation; it supports administrators but doesn't replace them. Security Copilot speeds up incident investigation in Microsoft Defender, Copilot in Intune summarizes and compares devices, explains policies and answers natural-language questions, and Intune agents help with guided tasks. Defender insights (incidents, device pages, advanced hunting, threat analytics, Secure Score) then drive Intune policy and remediation decisions.
objectives: Describe how AI transforms endpoint telemetry into prioritized recommendations and remediation actions
Investigate security incidents using Microsoft Security Copilot summaries, guided responses, script analysis, and promptbooks
Troubleshoot devices with Copilot in Intune by comparing devices, analyzing errors, and exploring policies
Analyze device performance and health trends using Endpoint Analytics
Use Microsoft Defender incidents, advanced hunting, threat analytics, and Secure Score to guide endpoint decisions
keyPoints: AI adds three things: **recommendations** (what to change), **prioritization** (what first) and **remediation** (doing it predictably). It reduces alert fatigue and gives operations and security teams a shared view.
**Security Copilot** in the Defender portal creates **incident summaries**, answers follow-up questions, gives **guided response**, analyzes scripts and generates hunting queries.
**Promptbooks** are reusable multi-prompt workflows that make repeated investigations consistent.
**Copilot in Intune** respects **RBAC and scope tags**: you only see data you're allowed to see.
**Compare devices** (working vs. failing) to narrow issues to targeting, filters, platform or conflicting settings.
**Intune Explorer** answers natural-language questions such as *Which Windows devices are noncompliant?*
Intune agents: **Change Review**, **Policy Configuration**, **Vulnerability Remediation**; the Device Offboarding agent is being retired.
**Always validate** AI output before high-impact actions, and pilot policy changes.

units.title: Understand the role of AI in modern endpoint management
points: AI correlates configuration, compliance, app, security, performance and user-experience signals and surfaces shared root causes.
Prioritization uses risk, severity, affected device count, user impact and compliance state.
Example recommendations: compliance policy for a threat, deploy a missing security setting, rerun a deployment after a transient error.
Shared context lets security validate the threat while operations executes the fix.

units.title: Use Microsoft Security Copilot to investigate threats
points: Incident summary: attack overview, timeline, affected assets, attack details, recommended actions; ask specific follow-up questions.
Guided response suggests containment such as isolating devices, AV scans, resetting credentials, revoking sessions, blocking files or IPs.
Script analysis decodes obfuscated PowerShell and extracts indicators (hashes, domains, IPs); validate against Defender evidence.
Generates queries to find related activity; promptbooks standardize investigations; reports for technical, executive and compliance audiences.

units.title: Use AI-powered recommendations in Microsoft Intune
points: Prompts: summarize device, show apps, policies, group memberships, primary user, analyze an error code.
Device comparison shows differences in hardware, compliance policies and assigned configurations.
Policy review: summarize a policy, explain settings, assess impact, prepare change-review notes.
Policy Configuration Agent turns requirements/standards into Settings Catalog policies; Change Review Agent runs with the setup admin's permissions.
Device Offboarding Agent: setup ended April 30, 2026; removed June 1, 2026.

units.title: Use Microsoft Defender insights to support endpoint decisions
points: A device can be enrolled and compliant yet still need action because of an incident or vulnerable software.
Incidents group related alerts, assets and evidence; device entity pages show risk, exposure, alerts and recommendations.
**Advanced hunting** queries up to 30 days of raw data; **Go hunt** pivots from an entity.
Threat analytics shows active campaigns and exposure; **Secure Score** measures security posture.
Resulting Intune actions: endpoint security policies, ASR rules, remediation scripts, patching, compliance review, isolate or reimage.

keyTerms.definition: AI assistant that summarizes incidents, answers questions, analyzes scripts and suggests responses.
Reusable set of prompts for a repeatable investigation workflow.
Natural-language assistance in the Intune admin center for devices, policies and errors, limited by RBAC and scope tags.
Natural-language search over Intune data that maps questions to query views.
Query-based threat hunting in Microsoft Defender over up to 30 days of raw data.
Measure of security posture; rises as recommended actions are completed.

tables.title: Security Copilot agents in Intune
rows: Reviews configuration and policy changes before deployment
Turns requirements and standards into Settings Catalog policies
Prioritizes and speeds up vulnerability remediation

remember: Copilot output is a **starting point** → confirm in reports and Defender evidence before acting.
Compliant ≠ safe → check **Defender** incidents and exposure too.
Copilot in Intune can't show what your role can't see → **RBAC and scope tags** apply.
Same investigation every time → use a **promptbook**.

selfCheck.q: One laptop gets a VPN profile and a similar one doesn't. Which Copilot capability helps fastest?
selfCheck.a: Compare devices in Copilot in Intune, which highlights differences in group membership, policies and attributes.

selfCheck.q: An incident includes encoded PowerShell. How can Security Copilot help?
selfCheck.a: Its script analysis decodes and explains the script and lists indicators such as hashes, domains and IPs, which you then validate against Defender evidence.

selfCheck.q: Which Defender tool lets you find every device that contacted a suspicious IP in the last weeks?
selfCheck.a: Advanced hunting, which queries up to 30 days of raw data.

modules.title: Monitor and optimize endpoint performance using Microsoft Intune
modules.learnSummary: Monitor endpoint performance and implement proactive remediation using Microsoft Intune and Endpoint analytics.
modules.tldr: Endpoint analytics is the main source of Windows performance data in Intune: startup performance, app reliability, device health, recommended actions and an overall score. Remediations (detection + remediation PowerShell script packages) fix recurring problems automatically, while update rings, Delivery Optimization and configuration policies reduce device load. Each change starts from a baseline, goes to a pilot group first, and is measured again afterwards.
objectives: Use Endpoint analytics to measure startup performance, app reliability, device health, and user experience.
Interpret analytics insights and prioritize the most impactful issues.
Create proactive remediation scripts that detect and fix common endpoint problems automatically.
Monitor reliability metrics and use them to improve endpoint stability.
Apply pilot testing and targeted deployment to reduce risk.
keyPoints: **Endpoint analytics** reports startup performance (boot and sign-in), app reliability (crashes, hangs), device health and **recommended actions**. Battery health needs extra licensing.
The **Endpoint analytics score** summarizes startup, app reliability and device health; start with the **lowest-scoring** devices.
**Remediations** = a script package with a **detection script** (exit `0` = OK, non-zero = fix needed) and a **remediation script**.
Create Remediations under **Devices > Manage devices > Scripts and remediations > Create script package**; scripts must be PowerShell and under **64 KB**.
Remediation scripts must be **safe to run repeatedly**; store them in source control with versioning and restricted edit rights.
**Device Query** runs real-time KQL against one Windows device for outliers; it's part of Advanced Analytics, which needs licensing on top of Intune Plan 1.
Reduce update impact with **update rings**, **Delivery Optimization** and update compliance monitoring; reduce load with power profiles, startup app management and **Storage Sense**.
Method: **baseline → pilot group → gradual rollout → measure**; prefer targeted remediation over broad device-wide changes.

units.title: Understand performance optimization in cloud-managed environments
points: Goals: faster boot and sign-in, reliable apps, fewer update/restart disruptions, less support effort.
Typical remediations: remove temp files, reset Windows Update components, clear Store cache, disable problematic startup apps.
Use Windows 10/11 update rings to stage updates and Delivery Optimization to limit network impact.
Configuration: power profiles, startup apps, limited background processing, Storage Sense.

units.title: Use Endpoint Analytics to optimize device performance
points: Open via **Devices > Monitor > Endpoint analytics**; filter the startup dashboard by device group to focus on pilots.
Recommended actions: disable high-impact startup apps, update drivers/firmware, optimize power settings, remove or repair software.
Insights-to-action loop: find top issues → pilot devices → map actions to policies or remediations → small group → monitor and adjust.
Device Query: **Devices > [device] > Device query** for slow-starting or crashing outliers.

units.title: Configure remediation scripts using Microsoft Intune
points: Remediations run on a schedule and fix issues before help desk involvement.
Detection returns 0 when no remediation is needed; the remediation script must run silently within the timeout.
Pilot on a group with varied hardware and update states; confirm remediation only runs where needed.
Monitor detected-issue counts, success/failure counts and script errors in the Endpoint analytics dashboard.
Avoid running high-impact remediations too often; document behavior and a rollback plan.

units.title: Monitor endpoint reliability and user experience with Endpoint Analytics
points: Metrics: app reliability, startup performance, device health (hardware/firmware readiness, Windows Update compatibility, file system), recommended actions.
Lower score = device likely needs intervention.
App reliability: find top crash/hang apps and check if isolated or widespread before changing configuration broadly.
Startup analysis distinguishes profile-loading delays from application startup.
Check metrics regularly, involve app owners, archive results.

keyTerms.definition: Single score summarizing startup performance, app reliability and device health.
Intune script packages with detection and remediation PowerShell scripts that run on a schedule.
Script that exits 0 when the device is healthy and non-zero when remediation is needed.
How much an app or service delays boot or sign-in.
Real-time KQL query against a single Windows device (Intune Suite or add-on).
Endpoint analytics guidance such as disabling startup apps or updating drivers.

remember: Recurring problem that keeps coming back → **Remediations** (scheduled detection + fix), not a manual fix per device.
Detection script exits **non-zero** → remediation runs; exit **0** → nothing happens.
Investigate one outlier device live → **Device Query**, not the aggregated dashboard.
Any optimization → **pilot group first**, then measure against the baseline.

selfCheck.q: Many devices have a broken Windows Update component that recurs. How do you fix it automatically?
selfCheck.a: Create a Remediations script package: a detection script that exits non-zero when the issue exists and a remediation script that resets the components, piloted first.

selfCheck.q: Endpoint analytics shows one device with very slow startup. How do you inspect its live state?
selfCheck.a: Use Device Query on that device (Devices > [device] > Device query), which is part of Advanced Analytics (licensed on top of Intune Plan 1).

selfCheck.q: Which devices should you address first in Endpoint analytics?
selfCheck.a: Those with the lowest Endpoint analytics scores, as they're most likely to drive support costs and productivity issues.

paths.title: Support operational excellence and readiness using Microsoft Intune
paths.summary: Learn how to implement reporting and data visibility, delegate administration using role-based access control, and maintain tenant health to keep your Microsoft Intune environment operationally ready.

modules.title: Implement reporting and data visibility using Microsoft Intune
modules.learnSummary: Access, customize, and share Microsoft Intune reports, workbooks, and dashboards to deliver actionable operational insights across your organization.
modules.tldr: Intune reports fall into organizational, operational, historical/trend and specialist categories, each for a different audience and data freshness. Filters, columns and saved views turn broad reports into actionable metrics, while Azure Monitor Workbooks provide shareable dashboards. Data leaves Intune through CSV export, Diagnostic Settings, the Data Warehouse or Graph automation — always with least privilege and data minimization.
objectives: Describe the categories of built-in Intune reports and their intended scope
Customize Intune report columns, filters, and saved views for actionable insights
Build and share workbooks and dashboards using Azure Monitor and the Intune admin center
Export, schedule, and securely share Intune reporting data with stakeholders
keyPoints: **Organizational** reports are tenant-wide and refresh on a schedule; **operational** reports are narrow, real-time views inside a workload for troubleshooting.
**Specialist** reporting uses the **Intune Data Warehouse OData feed** or **Azure Monitor workbooks** on **Log Analytics** when built-in reports aren't deep enough.
**Endpoint analytics** measures user experience (startup performance, app reliability, work-from-anywhere readiness); **Advanced Analytics** requires the **Intune Suite**.
Save combinations of filters and columns as **custom views** so you don't rebuild queries daily.
The **admin center Home dashboard** is personal and **can't be shared**; use Azure Monitor Workbooks or Power BI for shared visibility.
Workbooks require **Diagnostic Settings** routing Intune logs to a **Log Analytics workspace**; viewers need only **Log Analytics Reader**.
Intune has **no native scheduled email report** — automate with **Graph API** (Logic App, Automation runbook) or the **Graph PowerShell SDK**.
For portal report access grant **Reports Reader** or **Global Reader**, never Intune Administrator; export only the fields stakeholders need.

units.title: Understand built-in reporting options in Microsoft Intune
points: Four categories by audience and freshness: organizational, operational, historical and trend, specialist.
Device compliance report: compliant, noncompliant, in-grace period, not evaluated.
Device configuration report: success, failure or conflict per profile and which setting errors.
Windows updates report: update versions, failures and devices pending reboot; Defender Antivirus report: engine state, signatures, real-time protection, active malware.
Endpoint analytics covers Intune-managed, co-managed and tenant-attached Windows devices for proactive IT.

units.title: Customize Intune reports and filters for actionable insights
points: Filter by ownership (BYOD), OS version or Error state to isolate the scope of a problem.
Add columns like Primary User UPN or OS Version and save as a custom view.
Compliance trends reveal systemic issues, e.g. a new macOS release conflicting with the baseline.
Enrollment failures can expose Autopilot ESP timeouts; feature update reports filtered on Rollback/Failed show which device groups to pause.

units.title: Use Microsoft Intune workbooks and dashboards
points: Select **Edit** on the Home page to add widgets such as device assignment status, app installation status and device compliance.
Workbooks combine text, KQL queries and charts; templates include Windows Update for Business reports and enrollment activity.
Share a workbook: save to a resource group, assign Log Analytics Reader via Azure RBAC, then use **Share** to send the link.
Power BI can connect to Log Analytics for executive reports.

units.title: Export, schedule, and share reporting data securely
points: Manual **Export** creates a CSV of the filtered view; Diagnostic Settings stream JSON to Storage, Event Hubs or Log Analytics.
The Intune Data Warehouse keeps historical data (up to 30 days for most fact tables) for Power BI.
Schedule reports with a Logic App or Automation runbook calling Graph, or a Graph PowerShell script via Scheduled Task or Azure Automation.
Audit logs record manual exports; audit the sign-ins and permissions of app registrations used for automation.

keyTerms.definition: Tenant-wide summary refreshed on a schedule, for leadership and security officers.
Narrow real-time view inside a workload, for troubleshooting a user or device.
OData feed with historical Intune data, designed for Power BI and other reporting tools.
Shareable interactive report combining text, KQL queries and charts on Log Analytics data.
Routes Intune logs as JSON to Log Analytics, Storage or Event Hubs.
User-experience telemetry: startup performance, app reliability, work-from-anywhere readiness.

tables.title: Ways to get data out of Intune
rows: Continuous logs to Log Analytics, Storage, Event Hubs; longer retention

remember: Share a dashboard with a manager → **Azure Monitor Workbook + Log Analytics Reader**, not the personal Home dashboard.
Auditor needs to see reports in the portal → **Reports Reader** or **Global Reader**, never Intune Administrator.
Weekly emailed report → **Graph API automation**; there's no built-in scheduling.
Workbook shows no data → check **Diagnostic Settings** send logs to Log Analytics.

selfCheck.q: A helpdesk agent needs to see the real-time install status of one app for a user. Which report category?
selfCheck.a: An operational report inside the Apps workload.

selfCheck.q: You want to spot slow startups and failing drivers before users complain. Which feature?
selfCheck.a: Endpoint analytics.

selfCheck.q: HR wants a list of corporate phones. How do you share it securely?
selfCheck.a: Export only the needed fields (data minimization), filtering before generating the CSV, and avoid granting admin roles.

modules.title: Apply RBAC and admin delegation in Microsoft Intune
modules.learnSummary: Configure role-based access control, scope tags, role assignments, and auditing to delegate Microsoft Intune administration safely across your organization.
modules.tldr: Intune RBAC decides what an admin can do; scope tags decide which objects they can see. A role assignment ties together the role, the admin group (members), the groups they may target and the scope tags. Audit logs, Diagnostic Settings and Azure Monitor alerts let you track who changed what and catch configuration drift.
objectives: Describe how Microsoft Intune RBAC and scope tags partition admin permissions and visibility
Choose between direct and group-based role assignments for multi-admin environments
Configure scope tags and role assignments to delegate regional or business-unit administration
Audit admin actions and export Intune audit logs for monitoring and compliance
Detect and respond to configuration drift using audit logs and Azure Monitor alerts
keyPoints: **RBAC = permissions** (what actions); **scope tags = visibility** (which objects).
A **role assignment** combines the role, **members** (admin group), **scope groups** (who they can target) and **scope tags** (what they can see).
**Intune Role Administrator** is the only Intune role that can assign permissions to other admins.
Every object gets the **Default** scope tag; to hide it from general admins, **remove Default** and add a custom tag.
**Group-based assignment** to a **role-assignable group** is recommended; the setting is **permanent** and needs **Entra ID P1 or P2**.
**Direct assignment** suits only special cases such as break-glass accounts.
**Multi Admin Approval** requires a second admin to approve RBAC changes.
Audit logs (Tenant administration > Audit logs) record action, admin UPN, target and time; export via **Diagnostic settings** for retention and alerts.

units.title: Understand RBAC and scope tags in Microsoft Intune
points: A role is a container of permissions; use built-in roles or custom roles with a granular permission mix.
Built-in examples: Policy and Profile Manager, Endpoint Security Manager, Help Desk Operator, Application Manager, Read Only Operator, Endpoint Privilege Manager/Reader.
Tag the object and tag the role assignment; admins see only objects with matching tags.
Admins with the Default tag can see all untagged objects.

units.title: Assign roles and permissions for multi-admin environments
points: Direct assignment: Entra admin center > Roles & admins > role > Add assignments; simple but hard to audit and to scale.
Role-assignable group: cloud-only security group with **Microsoft Entra roles can be assigned to the group** = Yes.
Group benefits: multiple roles at once, auditing by membership, Access Reviews to remove stale admins.
Add a description and an owner to admin groups.

units.title: Configure scoped administration for regional or business unit separation
points: Step 1: create tags under Tenant administration > Roles > Scope (Tags) (requires Intune Administrator).
Step 2: tag profiles, policies and apps via Properties > Scope tags, removing Default where needed.
Step 3: Tenant administration > Roles > All roles > role > Assignments: admin groups, scope groups, scope tags.
Verify: the regional admin sees only tagged profiles and can only target groups in scope.
Best practices: consistent tag prefixes (`Loc-`, `Dept-`) and a central IT assignment with all scope tags.

units.title: Audit admin actions and monitor configuration changes
points: Audit logs track admin actions; operational logs track system behavior such as enrollment failures.
Intune keeps audit logs for a limited time (up to one year); export filtered views to CSV.
Diagnostic settings (Reports > Diagnostic settings, AuditLogs): Log Analytics for KQL and alerts, storage account for cheap archive, event hub for a third-party SIEM.
Detect drift with Azure Monitor alert rules (e.g. on `Delete DeviceCompliancePolicy`), monitoring scope tag changes and correlating with PIM activations.

keyTerms.definition: Role-based access control — defines which actions an admin can perform.
Label that limits which Intune objects an admin can see and modify.
The users or devices an admin in a role assignment is allowed to manage and target.
Cloud-only security group that can hold Entra roles; the property can't be changed later and needs Entra ID P1/P2.
Requires a second administrator to approve protected changes such as RBAC modifications.
Settings deviating from the established baseline through mistakes or malicious activity.

tables.title: Parts of an Intune role assignment

remember: Admin still sees another region's profile → the object still has the **Default** tag.
Admin can see the right objects but deploys to the wrong users → fix **Scope (Groups)**, not scope tags.
Who can delegate Intune RBAC itself → **Intune Role Administrator**.
Alert when a compliance policy is deleted → audit logs to **Log Analytics** + **Azure Monitor alert rule**.

selfCheck.q: You want admins to inherit Intune Administrator by group membership. What must the group be?
selfCheck.a: A cloud-only security group created with 'Microsoft Entra roles can be assigned to the group' set to Yes (requires Entra ID P1/P2).

selfCheck.q: A help desk member should reboot devices and reset passcodes but not delete policies. Which built-in role?
selfCheck.a: Help Desk Operator.

selfCheck.q: Audit logs must be kept for seven years cheaply. Which destination?
selfCheck.a: Archive to a storage account through Diagnostic settings.

modules.title: Maintain tenant health and support readiness
modules.learnSummary: Monitor Microsoft Intune tenant health, configure proactive alerts, use built-in support tools, and document changes to maintain operational readiness.
modules.tldr: Because Intune is SaaS, first check whether a problem is Microsoft's (service health) or yours (configuration). Configure alerts at three layers — device compliance, critical admin events via Azure Monitor, and service health — so the right team hears about issues first. Use the troubleshooting portal, client tools and the Support Assistant, and keep operational baselines plus a change log to spot and roll back drift.
objectives: Monitor Microsoft Intune tenant health and interpret service communications
Configure alerts and notifications for device compliance, system events, and service health
Use Intune support tools and troubleshoot service-related issues effectively
Document tenant changes and establish operational baselines to detect configuration drift
keyPoints: **Tenant administration > Tenant status** shows tenant details, connector status (Apple tokens, Managed Google Play) and service health; Microsoft 365 admin center > **Health > Service health** shows all M365 services.
**Service incident** = significant impact, stop local troubleshooting; **service advisory** = minor or intermittent degradation; **Message center** = upcoming changes, not outages.
**Tenant-specific action items** need admin intervention and the **Service support administrator** role.
Intune has **no native alert rules engine** for admin actions — route logs to **Log Analytics** and create **Azure Monitor alert rules**.
Service health emails: Microsoft 365 admin center > Health > Service health > **Customize** > Email.
Troubleshooting order: **service health → licensing and group membership → Troubleshoot pane → policy conflicts** (a conflict means neither setting applies).
On Windows, `dsregcmd /status` checks Entra join state; on mobile, Company Portal **Send Logs** returns an Incident ID.
Audit logs show what changed but not why; keep a **change log** with justification, approval and a **rollback plan**, compared weekly against **baselines**.

units.title: Monitor tenant health and Intune service communications
points: Distinguish your misconfiguration from a Microsoft outage before troubleshooting.
Message center announces deprecations, UI changes and new capabilities — use the lead time to update documentation.
Cadence: daily 60-second Tenant status check (connectors like Apple ADE, Autopilot), weekly Message center review.
Automate with email alerts from the Microsoft 365 admin center or route service health to a Teams channel via the Graph service communications API.

units.title: Configure alerts and notifications in Microsoft Intune
points: Three layers: compliance failures, critical events and config drift, service health.
Compliance: phased actions for noncompliance (push, email with helpdesk CC, final warning, Conditional Access block); emails need a notification message template.
Azure Monitor alert examples: active malware, `Delete DeviceConfiguration`/`Delete DeviceCompliancePolicy`, more than 10 devices unenrolled or wiped within an hour.
Service health email notifications can be chosen for Intune and related services, for incidents, advisories or both.

units.title: Use support tools and troubleshoot service-related issues
points: Troubleshooting + support > **Troubleshoot**: per-user view of licensing, compliance, apps and enrollment failures.
Windows: Access work or school > Info > **Sync**; Event Viewer DeviceManagement-Enterprise-Diagnostics-Provider > Admin; MDM diagnostics report locally or via **Collect diagnostics**.
**Support Assistant** (Help and support or the ? icon) is opt-in with panes Find solutions, Contact support and Service requests.
Severity drives response SLAs; Premier/Unified Support unlocks higher severity and scheduled callbacks.

units.title: Document tenant changes and establish operational baselines
points: Baselines to track: compliance rate, enrollment success, app deployment success, Endpoint analytics boot time and reliability.
Enrollment regressions often point to a broken ESP app package or expired APNs certificate.
Change log fields: date, change ID, admin, component, description, justification, expected impact, rollback plan (SharePoint list, Jira, ServiceNow, Excel).
Weekly cycle: compare baselines, correlate regressions with changes from the last 72 hours, execute rollback, verify in a test group.

keyTerms.definition: Intune admin center page with tenant details, connector status and service health.
Critical issue with significant user or admin impact that Microsoft is actively resolving.
Minor, intermittent or localized degradation while the core service works.
Microsoft's change-management channel for upcoming changes and deprecations.
Snapshot of normal health metrics used to detect regressions.
Record of tenant changes with justification, approval, impact and rollback plan.

tables.title: Service communications
rows: Stop local troubleshooting; follow the incident for resolution times
Be aware and inform the helpdesk
Issue in your tenant needing admin action

remember: Enrollments fail tenant-wide → check **Tenant status / Service health** before changing policies.
Alert when an admin deletes a policy → **Azure Monitor alert rule on Log Analytics**, not an Intune setting.
Two policies set different PIN lengths → **Conflict**, and **neither** applies.
Audit log answers who/what/when; the **change log** answers why and how to roll back.

selfCheck.q: A Windows device stopped syncing policies. Which command checks whether it still trusts Microsoft Entra ID?
selfCheck.a: `dsregcmd /status` — verify AzureAdJoined (or EnterpriseJoined) is YES.

selfCheck.q: Reporting data is delayed by two hours but Intune otherwise works. What type of communication is this?
selfCheck.a: A service advisory.

selfCheck.q: Compliance dropped from 96% to 88% overnight. What is your first step?
selfCheck.a: Check the change log for changes in the last 72 hours affecting compliance or Conditional Access, then roll back using the documented plan.

paths.title: Extend endpoint capabilities using Microsoft Intune Suite
paths.summary: Learn how to extend Microsoft Intune with the Microsoft Intune Suite, including Remote Help, Endpoint Privilege Management, Advanced Endpoint Analytics, and other premium endpoint management capabilities.

modules.title: Explore Microsoft Intune Suite capabilities
modules.learnSummary: Identify Microsoft Intune Suite add-on components, evaluate how they extend core Intune capabilities, and plan licensing and deployment strategies for advanced endpoint management scenarios.
modules.tldr: The Microsoft Intune Suite is a set of premium add-ons on top of core Intune for advanced management, security and support scenarios. Its eight components — from Endpoint Privilege Management and Remote Help to Cloud PKI — can be licensed individually or as one package. Plan with a 90-day trial, pilot groups and correct per-user license assignment.
objectives: Describe the purpose and business value of the Microsoft Intune Suite
Identify the key components of the Intune Suite, including Remote Help, Endpoint Privilege Management, and Advanced Analytics
Compare Intune Suite features to core Microsoft Intune capabilities
Plan licensing options and deployment strategies for Intune Suite add-ons
keyPoints: **Core Intune** covers enrollment, configuration, apps, compliance, Conditional Access, basic reporting and RBAC; the **Intune Suite** adds premium capabilities for advanced scenarios.
Eight add-ons: **EPM, Remote Help, Advanced Analytics, Enterprise App Management, Tunnel for MAM, Cloud PKI, FOTA, specialty devices management**.
**Endpoint Privilege Management** lets standard users elevate approved apps via rules, using an isolated **virtual account** — least privilege without productivity loss.
**Microsoft Tunnel for MAM** is the only add-on that works on **unenrolled** Android and iOS devices (app-level VPN for BYOD).
**Licensing**: individual add-ons (per user), the full Intune Suite (includes future add-ons), or some add-ons via **Intune Plan 2**.
**Trials** last 90 days, up to 250 users, one trial per add-on per tenant, plus a 30-day grace period (120 days total); started by Global or Billing administrators.
**Remote Help** needs licenses for both **helpers and sharers**; EPM licenses go to the users who elevate, not to admins who only manage policies.
Roll out in **phases**: pilot groups first (EPM tip: 10–20 users from one department for 2–4 weeks), then expand.

units.title: Understand the purpose and value of the Microsoft Intune Suite
points: The Intune Suite is a collection of premium add-ons extending core Intune; license individually or as a complete package.
Business value per component: least privilege (EPM), secure remote assistance (Remote Help), proactive management (Advanced Analytics), streamlined Win32 apps (Enterprise App Management).
Also: BYOD connectivity (Tunnel for MAM), certificate automation (Cloud PKI), firmware updates (FOTA) and purpose-built devices (specialty devices management).
Supports Zero Trust: verify explicitly, use least privilege access, assume breach.

units.title: Identify key components of the Microsoft Intune Suite
points: EPM elevation types: automatic, user-confirmed, support-approved, elevate as current user, plus deny rules; reports separate managed from unmanaged elevations.

Remote Help: helper and sharer sign in with organizational Entra accounts (same tenant only); compliance warnings shown before connecting; Windows adds elevation, remote launch and optional unenrolled support.
Advanced Analytics: anomaly detection, predictive insights, recommendations, **Device Query** (real-time KQL) and **Battery Health**.
Enterprise App Catalog: pre-configured Win32 apps hosted in Microsoft storage; Cloud PKI automates issuance, renewal and revocation.
FOTA currently supports Zebra devices (LifeGuard Over-the-Air); specialty devices management covers AR/VR headsets, smart screens and meeting-room devices.

units.title: Compare Microsoft Intune Suite features to core Intune capabilities
points: Core Intune has remote actions (lock, wipe, sync, restart) but no screen sharing or remote control — that's Remote Help.
Core Intune can run deployments with system privileges, but can't let users elevate specific apps on demand — that's EPM.
Core reporting is reactive; Advanced Analytics is proactive (anomalies, predictions).
Core Intune still deploys Win32 apps; Enterprise App Management only cuts the preparation work for catalog apps.
Core Microsoft Tunnel requires enrollment; Tunnel for MAM doesn't.

units.title: Plan licensing and deployment strategies for the Microsoft Intune Suite
points: Trials via **Tenant administration > Intune add-ons > All add-ons**, completed in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
Assign licenses per user or with group-based licensing on Entra groups; unlicensed users can't use the features even if configured.
Check prerequisites: network endpoints, OS versions, Intune enrollment and Entra ID integration.
Plan change management, help desk training and regular license reviews (reclaim unused licenses).
Sovereign cloud (e.g. GCC) availability varies per add-on.

keyTerms.definition: Package of premium Intune add-ons, licensed individually or together, extending core Intune.
Lets standard users run approved apps elevated based on admin-defined rules.
Curated set of pre-configured, Microsoft-hosted Win32 apps for Intune deployment.
App-level VPN through Microsoft Tunnel for unenrolled Android and iOS devices.
Cloud-hosted PKI that issues, renews and revokes certificates for Intune-managed devices.
Firmware Over-the-Air: remote firmware updates for supported specialty devices (Zebra).

tables.title: Core Intune vs Intune Suite add-on
rows: Remote actions: lock, wipe, sync, restart
Remote Help: screen sharing, full control, elevation, auditing
EPM: standard users elevate approved apps
Advanced Analytics: anomalies, predictions, Device Query
Tunnel for MAM on unenrolled Android/iOS

remember: Personal phones, no enrollment, need VPN → **Tunnel for MAM**, the only Suite add-on not requiring an enrolled device.
Trial = **90 days + 30-day grace**, max 250 users, **one trial per add-on per tenant**.
Remote Help licensing → **both helper and sharer**; EPM licensing → the **elevating users**, not policy admins.
Lock/wipe/restart are **core Intune**; screen sharing and control are **Remote Help**.

selfCheck.q: A company wants to stop maintaining its on-premises certificate authority for device certificates. Which Intune Suite component fits?
selfCheck.a: Cloud PKI, which automates certificate issuance, renewal and revocation as a cloud service.

selfCheck.q: Your tenant's EPM trial expired last year and you want to evaluate it again. Can you start a new trial?
selfCheck.a: No — each tenant can start only one trial per add-on.

selfCheck.q: You plan to use several add-ons and want new capabilities included as they're released. Which licensing option fits?
selfCheck.a: The complete Intune Suite, which includes all current add-ons plus new ones Microsoft adds.

modules.title: Implement Remote Help scenarios using Microsoft Intune
modules.learnSummary: Configure and deploy Microsoft Intune Remote Help, assign helper and sharer permissions, monitor support sessions, and evaluate privacy considerations for managed remote support.
modules.tldr: Remote Help is an Intune Suite capability for secure, interactive support: an approved helper views the user's screen and, with consent, takes control or handles elevation prompts. Access is tied to Entra ID identities in the same tenant and controlled with Intune RBAC. Sessions are monitored through Intune reports and audit logs, which store only metadata — never recordings or keystrokes.
objectives: Describe the purpose of Remote Help in end-user support
Identify the helper, sharer, and administrator roles in a Remote Help workflow
Configure Remote Help in the Microsoft Intune admin center and deploy the app to supported platforms
Assign Remote Help permissions by using Intune role-based access control
Support and monitor Remote Help sessions
Evaluate privacy, permission, and compliance considerations for remote support
keyPoints: **Remote Help** is **disabled by default**; enable it under **Tenant administration > Remote Help > Settings**.
Helper and sharer both sign in with **organizational Entra ID accounts** in the **same tenant** — cross-tenant sessions aren't supported.
**Licenses** are needed for **both helpers and sharers**, on top of Intune Plan 1 or Plan 2; new licenses can take 30 minutes to several hours to apply.
A helper needs **Offer remote assistance**, **Remote Assistance Connector – Read** and at least one app permission: **View screen, Take full control, Elevation or Unattended**.
The built-in **Help Desk Operator** role includes the Remote Help permissions; use **custom roles** and **scope groups** for least privilege.
**Elevation** (UAC prompts) is Windows-only and privileged; **Unattended** is only for supported Android Enterprise **dedicated devices**.
The user sees the helper's identity, **approves** screen sharing or full control, and either party can end the session.
Only **session metadata** (who, which device, times, features used) is kept, for up to **30 days**; no screen images, recordings or keystrokes.

units.title: Understand Remote Help and its role in end-user support
points: Supports screen sharing, file transfer and privileged escalation; a session can start with a one-time session code.
Use it when the agent needs screen-level visibility and an auditable workflow — not as a meeting or collaboration tool.
Roles: device user (sharer, approves the session), support agent (helper, needs Intune RBAC permissions), administrator (configures settings, assigns roles, reviews logs).
RBAC scope controls which users or devices a helper can support.

units.title: Configure and deploy Remote Help with Microsoft Intune
points: Platforms: Windows, Windows 365, Azure Virtual Desktop, macOS, Android Enterprise dedicated devices and the web app.
Tenant settings: **Allow Remote Help to unenrolled devices** (less context and auditing) and **Disable chat**.
If the sharer or device is outside the helper's RBAC scope, no help is possible; for unenrolled devices use **user** scope groups (All Devices excludes them).
Windows: deploy via Enterprise App Catalog or as Win32 app; needs WebView2 Runtime, and remote launch needs the Intune management extension.
macOS: native app needed for full control (web app = screen sharing only); Android: deploy from Managed Google Play, camera permission required.

units.title: Support and monitor Remote Help sessions
points: Start with screen sharing; request full control only when the helper must interact directly.
**Tenant administration > Remote Help**: the Monitor tab shows active and historical sessions; the Remote Help sessions tab shows past sessions.
Troubleshoot with **Tenant administration > Audit logs**: device offline, missing role, or user declined elevation.
Check that the device is enrolled and healthy, the app is up to date and the helper has the right permissions.

units.title: Evaluate privacy, permission, and compliance considerations
points: Before connecting, the user sees the helper's name, company, verified domain and job title.
Grant elevation only to roles that need it; disable unattended access for normal user support.
Compliance checks: verify identities, scope, view-only vs full control, and failed sessions against tickets.
Review regularly who can help, which groups can receive help and whether unenrolled support is still allowed.

keyTerms.definition: Support agent who connects to a device; needs a license and Intune RBAC permissions.
The device user receiving help; needs a license and approves screen sharing or control.
Built-in Intune role that includes the required Remote Help permissions.
Remote Help permission letting the helper interact with Windows UAC prompts.
Permission to connect to supported Android Enterprise dedicated devices without the sharer accepting each time.

tables.title: Remote Help app permissions
rows: See the sharer's screen without control
Connect to Android Enterprise dedicated devices without acceptance each time

remember: Helper can't connect even though licensed → check **RBAC scope**; for unenrolled devices use **user** scope groups.
Remote Help records **metadata only** (30 days) — **no** screen recordings or keystrokes.
Unattended access → **Android Enterprise dedicated devices**, not regular Windows user support.
Supporting another company's tenant → **not possible**; Remote Help is single-tenant.

selfCheck.q: First-line support should only see users' screens, while a small senior team may approve UAC prompts. How do you configure this?
selfCheck.a: Create custom Intune roles: one with View screen only, another with Take full control and Elevation, each scoped to the right groups.

selfCheck.q: A helper wants to use Remote Help for a device that isn't enrolled in Intune. What must be in place?
selfCheck.a: The tenant setting Allow Remote Help to unenrolled devices must be enabled, and the helper's scope must use user scope groups.

selfCheck.q: An auditor asks for a recording of last week's Remote Help session. Can you provide one?
selfCheck.a: No. Remote Help keeps only session metadata such as who, which device, times and features used, for up to 30 days.

modules.title: Analyze advanced device signals with Microsoft Intune Suite
modules.learnSummary: Use Microsoft Intune Suite Advanced Analytics, anomaly detection, and integration with Microsoft Defender to surface real-time device health and risk signals and drive risk-based policy decisions.
modules.tldr: Intune Advanced Analytics (Intune Suite or standalone add-on) moves reporting from static compliance to real-time health: live KQL Device Query, machine-learning anomaly detection, resource performance and battery insights. Integrating Intune with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint adds a live machine risk score that drives risk-based compliance and Conditional Access. Together these signals let you adapt policies to a device's actual risk and health.
objectives: Explore advanced reporting with Microsoft Intune Suite Advanced Analytics
Identify and respond to anomaly detection insights
Integrate Intune data with Microsoft Defender for proactive threat signals
Use advanced insights to support risk-based compliance and Conditional Access policy decisions
keyPoints: **Advanced Analytics** requires the standalone Advanced Analytics add-on or the **Microsoft Intune Suite**.
**Device Query** runs live **KQL** queries against devices and answers in seconds, instead of waiting for inventory sync.
**Anomaly detection** uses machine learning to baseline "normal" for your tenant and flags deviations by **severity** (High, Medium, Low) — no manual thresholds.
Investigate anomalies with **Correlations** (shared model or OS version) and the **Device Timeline**; **Mute** anomalies you don't need to act on to avoid alert fatigue.
Intune deploys Defender onboarding to devices; **Defender** sends back a **machine risk score** — a two-way signal flow.
**Risk-based compliance**: a compliance rule requiring risk Clear/Low marks a High-risk device **noncompliant**, and **Conditional Access** blocks access until the risk clears.
**Security tasks**: SecOps sends a remediation request from the Defender portal; IT sees it under **Endpoint security > Security tasks** and Defender closes it after the fix.
**Custom compliance** policies run a PowerShell (Windows) or Bash (macOS) discovery script returning JSON to base compliance on your own signals.

units.title: Explore advanced reporting with Intune Suite analytics
points: Device Query: live KQL across Windows and macOS devices, e.g. to find machines running a vulnerable service right now.
Anomaly Detection flags deviations such as a crash spike on one hardware model after an update.
EPM reporting shows what users try to elevate; use it to build targeted elevation rules instead of granting local admin.
Resource Performance: fleet-wide CPU, memory and disk performance for enrolled Windows devices.

units.title: Identify and respond to anomaly detection insights
points: How it works: baselining telemetry (app reliability, boot times, crashes) → machine-learning model → anomaly on deviation.
Find them under **Reports > Endpoint analytics > Anomalies**; the State column shows Active or Resolved.
Respond: review details → Correlations → Device Timeline → remediate (pause update rings, alert help desk, test a fix on a small group).
Mute anomalies for apps known to be unstable or being deprecated.

units.title: Integrate Intune with Microsoft Defender for proactive threat signals
points: Connector: **Tenant administration > Connectors and tokens > Microsoft Defender for Endpoint**; enable Windows (10 1809+ and 11) and iOS/iPadOS and Android (Mobile Threat Defense).
Turn on **Allow Microsoft Defender for Endpoint to enforce Endpoint Security Configurations**.
Add a Defender for Endpoint rule in compliance policies requiring a maximum machine risk score (typically Clear or Low).
The connector only builds the pipeline — you still need an **EDR policy** in Intune to onboard devices.
When the threat is remediated, the score returns to Clear, the device becomes compliant and access is restored.

units.title: Use advanced insights to support risk-based policy decisions
points: Risk-based policy is a sliding scale: slightly elevated risk → Conditional Access requires MFA; High risk → access blocked.
Endpoint analytics insights (app reliability, battery health, anomalies) inform actions like pausing update rings or running Remediations scripts.
Custom compliance scripts can check e.g. a vulnerable registry key; noncompliant devices are blocked by Conditional Access.
Microsoft Security Copilot's Intune plugin answers natural-language questions on live Intune data; it needs separately licensed SCU capacity.
If an agent is unstable, temporarily switch its compliance check from Require to Report-only to avoid mass lockouts.

keyTerms.definition: Real-time KQL query against managed devices for current property data.
Machine-learning baseline of normal device behavior that flags deviations by severity.
Dynamic device risk level calculated by Defender for Endpoint and shared with Intune.
Compliance based on the live Defender risk score rather than static settings.
Defender vulnerability remediation requests that appear in Intune under Endpoint security.
Compliance policy based on a PowerShell or Bash discovery script that outputs JSON.

tables.title: Anomaly severity levels
rows: Critical issue affecting many devices or severe disruption (e.g. frequent BSODs); act immediately
Noticeable degradation without halting productivity (e.g. more app hangs)

remember: Need an answer from devices **right now** → **Device Query (KQL)**, not standard hardware inventory.
Defender connector enabled but devices not in Defender → you still need an **EDR policy** to onboard them.
Static compliance asks "should it be secure?"; **risk-based compliance** asks "is it secure right now?" via the machine risk score.
Vulnerability fix handoff from SecOps to IT → **Security tasks** in Intune, not a spreadsheet.

selfCheck.q: Defender detects malware on a laptop and raises its risk score to High. What happens if the compliance policy requires Low or Clear?
selfCheck.a: Intune marks the device noncompliant and Conditional Access blocks access to corporate resources until the risk returns to Clear.

selfCheck.q: After a Windows update, Advanced Analytics flags a High anomaly of VPN crashes on one laptop model. What are sensible first steps?
selfCheck.a: Check Correlations and the Device Timeline to find the cause, then pause the update ring, alert the help desk and test a fix on a small group.

selfCheck.q: Your security team needs compliance to depend on a specific registry key that native settings don't cover. What do you use?
selfCheck.a: A custom compliance policy with a PowerShell discovery script that returns the result in JSON.

modules.title: Evaluate Endpoint Privilege Management with Microsoft Intune
modules.learnSummary: Evaluate Microsoft Intune Endpoint Privilege Management — design just-in-time elevation, configure elevation policies, monitor elevated actions, and troubleshoot and refine the deployment.
modules.tldr: Endpoint Privilege Management (EPM) removes permanent local admin rights and lets standard users run approved files, installers or scripts with just-in-time elevation. You configure it with two Intune policies: an elevation settings policy (enables EPM, default response, reporting) and an elevation rules policy (per-file rules and elevation types). Reports and support-approved requests help you find gaps and refine the rule set.
objectives: Describe the role of Endpoint Privilege Management in Zero Trust endpoint strategies
Understand just-in-time elevation in EPM
Configure EPM elevation policies and rules in the Microsoft Intune admin center
Monitor elevated actions and review elevation reports
Troubleshoot and refine an EPM deployment
keyPoints: **Just-in-time elevation**: users stay standard users; EPM allows, denies or routes each elevation request according to policy.
Most elevations run under an isolated **virtual account** — neither it nor the user is added to local Administrators; **Elevate as current user** is the exception.
Two policies: **elevation settings policy** (enables EPM, default response, reporting scope) and **elevation rules policy** (rules per file). Rules do nothing without the settings policy.
Secure **default elevation response**: **Deny all requests** or **Require support approval**; Require user confirmation applies to all unmatched files, so use it carefully.
Elevation types: **Automatic, User confirmed, Support approved, Deny, Elevate as current user**.
Precedence: **Deny wins**, **user-targeted beats device-targeted**, rules with a **hash** are more specific.
Child process default: **Require rule to elevate**; "Allow all child processes" skips rule evaluation, including deny rules.

Requirements: add-on license on top of Intune Plan 1/2, supported Windows 10/11, **Entra joined or hybrid joined**, Intune-enrolled or co-managed; **no SSL inspection**, **workplace joined not supported**.

units.title: Understand just-in-time elevation in Endpoint Privilege Management
points: Local admin rights let users and attackers change system settings; EPM limits elevation to defined conditions (Zero Trust).
Benefits: fewer permanent admins, approved admin tasks without changing account type, control of what elevates, recorded activity.
Supports Windows 365 and Azure Virtual Desktop single-session VMs; unsupported OS versions report **Not applicable**.
Required EPM traffic must bypass SSL inspection.

units.title: Configure elevation policies and rules
points: Create both under **Endpoint security > Endpoint Privilege Management > Policies > Create**, platform Windows.
Reporting scope options: diagnostic data only, managed elevations only, or all endpoint elevations.
Rules identify files by name, path, signature source/certificate or hash, minimum version and metadata; use paths standard users can't modify.
**Reusable settings groups** store a publisher certificate used across multiple rules.
Rules can be created directly from the Elevation report or a support-approved request; policies can target users or devices.

units.title: Monitor elevated actions and review reports
points: Reports under **Endpoint security > Endpoint Privilege Management > Reports**: Elevation report, Managed elevation report, by application, by publisher, by user, Denied elevation report.
**Unmanaged elevations** (e.g. an admin using Run as administrator) reveal gaps in your model.
Support-approved requests are handled on the **Elevation requests** tab; once approved, the user can retry for **24 hours**.
Denied requests aren't notified automatically — tell the user through the normal support process.

units.title: Troubleshoot and refine an EPM deployment
points: Settings policy errors or Not applicable: often missing Windows updates or blocked Intune endpoints.
Rule mismatch causes: wrong path, updated file (hash/version changed), changed certificate, missing required arguments, wrong assignment.
Only local files elevate — files on network shares or mapped drives aren't supported.
Elevated apps run in an isolated context and can't reach resources needing user authentication (network shares, OneDrive, SharePoint, Azure).

keyTerms.definition: Elevated privileges only for a specific approved task, without making the user a permanent admin.
Isolated account EPM uses to run most elevated processes, separate from the signed-in user.
Enables EPM and sets the default elevation response and reporting.
Defines per-file rules and their elevation type and child process behavior.
What happens to elevation requests for files that match no rule.
Elevation outside EPM, such as a local admin using Run as administrator.

tables.title: EPM elevation types
rows: Highly trusted files with strong criteria (hash, certificate, path, version)
User prompt; optional justification and/or Windows authentication
Admin must approve the request first
Runs under the signed-in user's account
App needs the user profile or context

tables.title: Child process behavior
rows: Child needs its own matching rule (preferred)
Allow all child processes to run elevated
Children elevate without rule evaluation, even deny rules
No child processes created or elevated

remember: Rules assigned but nothing happens → device also needs an **elevation settings policy** enabling EPM.
Two rules conflict → **Deny wins**, then **user-targeted over device-targeted**, then the more specific **hash** rule.
Elevated app can't open SharePoint or a network share → **expected EPM limitation** (isolated context), not a broken rule.
Workplace joined (registered) device → **EPM not supported**; needs Entra joined or hybrid joined.

selfCheck.q: You want unknown applications never to elevate unless a support engineer reviews them. Which default elevation response do you choose?
selfCheck.a: Require support approval (or Deny all requests if requests shouldn't be possible at all).

selfCheck.q: A user's approved support request worked yesterday, but today the elevation fails again. Why?
selfCheck.a: An approved request only lets the user retry elevation for that file for 24 hours.

selfCheck.q: An EPM rule stopped matching after the vendor released a new version of the tool. What's the likely cause?
selfCheck.a: The rule's file hash or version no longer matches the updated file; update the rule or use certificate-based criteria.

paths.title: Deliver cloud-hosted desktops using Azure Virtual Desktop and Windows 365
paths.summary: Learn how to plan, deploy, and manage cloud-hosted desktops using Windows 365 and Azure Virtual Desktop, and integrate Cloud PCs and Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts with Microsoft Intune.

modules.title: Explore Windows 365 for cloud PC deployment
modules.learnSummary: Explore Windows 365 — its role for cloud PC deployment, how it compares to traditional VDI, licensing and prerequisites, common use cases, and endpoint experience options like Windows 365 Boot and Switch.
modules.tldr: Windows 365 is a SaaS service that streams persistent, personalized Cloud PCs from Microsoft-managed Azure infrastructure, managed through Intune and secured with Entra ID. Compared with traditional PCs and VDI, it removes imaging, host-pool and infrastructure work. Choose the right plan (Business, Enterprise, Frontline, Flex), network model and access experience (Windows App/browser, Windows 365 Boot, Windows 365 Switch).
objectives: Describe the role of Windows 365 in delivering cloud-hosted Windows desktops
Compare Windows 365 to traditional virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI)
Identify Windows 365 licensing, service plans, and prerequisites
Identify common Windows 365 use cases
Explore Windows 365 endpoint experience options, including Windows 365 Boot and Windows 365 Switch
keyPoints: A **Cloud PC** is **persistent**: apps, settings and files remain between sessions, just like a physical PC.
**Shared responsibility**: Microsoft runs the Cloud PC infrastructure and availability; you manage users, licenses, apps, identity and security policies.
Plans: **Business** (SMB, simple), **Enterprise** (Intune integration, custom networking, GPU options), **Frontline** (shift workers, concurrent use), **Flex** (intermittent use).
**Frontline**: license for the **maximum concurrent users** — e.g. 15 associates across shifts, never more than 5 at once → 5 licenses.
**Flex Dedicated**: one license provisions up to **three** personal Cloud PCs, one active session at a time; **Flex Shared**: one license = one shared Cloud PC, no data persistence required.
Networking: **Microsoft Hosted Network** (recommended, no Azure subscription) or **Azure Network Connection** (needed for **hybrid join** or line-of-sight to on-prem resources).
The **Windows App** is the recommended client and successor to the Remote Desktop app; a browser is a fallback for unmanaged or shared devices.
**Windows 365 Boot** signs users straight into the Cloud PC (thin-client style); **Windows 365 Switch** toggles local and Cloud PC via **Task View** — both need **Windows 11 22H2+**.

units.title: Understand the role of Windows 365
points: Integrations: Entra ID (identity), Intune (management and compliance), Azure networking, Microsoft Defender (security).
Identity-centered security with Conditional Access, MFA, compliance policies and Defender supports Zero Trust; data stays in the cloud even from personal devices.
Management in the Intune admin center: provisioning policies, apps, profiles, device actions (restart, reprovision, resize, restore).
Removes imaging, VDI design, session host and capacity management, and platform patching.

units.title: Compare Windows 365 to traditional VDI
points: Traditional PCs: full offline capability and hardware access, but imaging, repairs and refresh cycles.
VDI: centralized, pooled or persistent desktops, but needs virtualization hosts, storage, networking and capacity planning.
Windows 365: automatic user-based provisioning, always persistent, managed with Intune, predictable per-user subscription.
Best fit: offline work and specialized hardware → physical PCs; hybrid work, BYOD and rapid onboarding → Windows 365.

units.title: Identify Windows 365 licensing, service plans, and prerequisites
points: Users need an Entra ID account, the right Windows 365 license, internet connectivity and a supported client.
Enterprise offers GPU-enabled Cloud PCs for CAD, 3D, media and visualization — higher cost, assign only when needed.
Admin roles: **Windows 365 Administrator** (Enterprise and Business), **Cloud PC Administrator**, **Cloud PC Reader** (read-only), Intune Administrator; use least privilege.
Access from Windows, macOS, iOS/iPadOS, Android and supported browsers.

units.title: Identify Windows 365 use cases
points: Hybrid/remote work and BYOD: corporate data stays in the Cloud PC; Conditional Access enforces MFA and compliance.
Contractors and temporary staff: provision within hours, remove access immediately when the engagement ends.
Privileged access workstations: dedicated Cloud PCs with security baselines, BitLocker, ASR rules, app control and EDR.
Also onboarding on day one, business continuity after hardware failure or office outage, and training labs.
Not ideal for offline needs, specialized hardware or performance-sensitive apps.

units.title: Explore the Windows 365 endpoint experience
points: Standard access (Windows App or browser): broadest device support — remote workers, contractors, BYOD.
Boot: power on → sign in → connected to the Cloud PC; for frontline, shared devices, call centers, hot-desking.
Switch: move between local and cloud desktops in Task View; for knowledge workers, developers, admins who need local resources.
All are configured through Intune; organizations can combine experiences per persona.

keyTerms.definition: Persistent, personalized Windows desktop streamed from Microsoft's cloud via Windows 365.
Plan for shift workers licensed by concurrent use; users have their own Cloud PC but not simultaneously.
Plan for intermittent use with Dedicated mode (up to 3 Cloud PCs per license) or Shared mode.
Recommended network option where Microsoft manages the network; no Azure subscription needed.
Customer-managed option connecting Cloud PCs to an Azure VNet, required for hybrid join or on-prem access.
Boot logs straight into the Cloud PC; Switch toggles local and Cloud PC through Task View.

tables.title: Windows 365 plans
rows: Dedicated Cloud PC per user, simplified
Small and medium organizations with limited management needs
Dedicated Cloud PC per user, full Intune integration
Centralized provisioning, custom networking, compliance, GPU workloads
Shift workers who never all work at the same time
Dedicated (up to 3 Cloud PCs/license) or Shared mode
Occasional, scheduled or on-demand use; training, temporary access

tables.title: Access experiences
rows: Launch a Cloud PC session from an app or portal
Remote workers, contractors, cross-platform and BYOD
Sign directly into the Cloud PC at startup
Switch between local and Cloud PC in Task View

remember: Cloud PC needs **hybrid Entra join** or direct on-prem access → **Azure Network Connection**, not Microsoft Hosted Network.
Shift workers sharing capacity → **Frontline** (concurrency); occasional users → **Flex**.
Device should act like a thin client → **Boot**; user needs both local and cloud desktops → **Switch**.
Windows 365 is **always persistent**; VDI can be persistent or nonpersistent.

selfCheck.q: A hospital has 60 nurses over three shifts, with at most 20 working at once. Which Windows 365 plan minimizes licensing cost?
selfCheck.a: Windows 365 Frontline, licensed for 20 concurrent users.

selfCheck.q: Cloud PCs must reach on-premises file servers and be hybrid Entra joined. Which network option do you choose?
selfCheck.a: Azure Network Connection, the customer-managed option linking Cloud PCs to an Azure virtual network and on-prem resources.

selfCheck.q: An administrator should only view Cloud PC information in Intune, without making changes. Which role do you assign?
selfCheck.a: Cloud PC Reader.

modules.title: Configure and manage Windows 365 with Microsoft Intune
modules.learnSummary: Configure Windows 365 provisioning policies, assign and manage Cloud PCs, apply configuration profiles and security policies, and monitor Cloud PC usage, performance, and health with Microsoft Intune.
modules.tldr: Intune is the management layer for Windows 365: a provisioning policy (join type, network, image, settings) assigned to an Entra user group creates Cloud PCs for licensed users. After provisioning you manage Cloud PCs like other Windows devices — remote actions, configuration profiles and the Windows 365 Security Baseline. Utilization, connection quality and resource performance reports show whether Cloud PCs are used, healthy and correctly sized.
objectives: Set up Windows 365 provisioning policies in Microsoft Intune
Assign and manage Cloud PCs
Apply configuration profiles and policies to Cloud PCs
Monitor Cloud PC usage, performance, and health
