keyPoints: A **provisioning policy** defines experience type, license type, **join type**, network, **image**, language/region, naming and optional services; no policy → user shows **Not provisioned**.
**Hybrid Entra join** requires an **Azure network connection**; Microsoft Entra join can use the **Microsoft-hosted network** (no Azure subscription).
Assign provisioning policies to **Entra user groups** — **nested groups aren't supported**; with overlapping policies the **first assigned** one wins.
**Grace period**: after a license or assignment change the user keeps the Cloud PC for **7 days**, then it's deprovisioned; ending it manually deletes the OS and data.
**Pending** = not enough licenses; **Provisioned with warnings** = usable but a non-critical step failed.
**Resize** keeps the Cloud PC (15–20 min downtime); **Restore** returns to a restore point; **Reprovision** rebuilds from the policy and erases data, apps and settings.
Target Cloud PCs with a **dynamic device group** on `deviceModel` starting with "Cloud PC", `enrollmentProfileName` per provisioning policy, or **Intune filters**.
Monitor with **Cloud PC utilization**, **Connection quality**, connectivity health checks, user connectivity history and **Resource performance** (Endpoint analytics).

units.title: Set up Windows 365 provisioning policies
points: Create under **Devices > Provision Cloud PCs > Provisioning policies > Create policy**.
Experience: full Cloud PC desktop, or only apps (Cloud Apps, for Flex Shared mode); license types include Enterprise, Frontline and Reserve.
Image: **gallery image** for a standard experience, **custom image** for organization-specific apps and settings.
Device name template must include a randomized string; optional services include Windows Autopatch and Windows Autopilot device preparation (installs selected apps and scripts during provisioning).

units.title: Assign and manage Cloud PCs
points: Flow: assign license → add user to the policy's group → Windows 365 provisions → verify. In a group but no Enterprise license → no Cloud PC.
User settings: enable local admin, allow user reset (wipes and reprovisions), allow user-initiated restore, cross-region disaster recovery; changes apply at next sign-in.
Access via the **Windows App** or windows.cloud.microsoft; **Windows 365 Link** is a dedicated device that Entra joins and enrolls in Intune.
Bulk remote actions: up to **5,000** Cloud PCs at a time, using a **user** group, not a device group.

units.title: Apply configuration profiles and policies to Cloud PCs
points: Create profiles under **Devices > Configuration > Create > New policy**; settings catalog for precise control, templates for grouped scenarios.
Typical areas: restrictions, Edge, OneDrive, Windows Update, Defender, Windows Hello for Business, network/VPN/certificates.
The **Windows 365 Security Baseline** (Endpoint security > Security baselines) covers Windows, Edge and Defender settings and can be customized.
Baseline profiles don't auto-update to new versions — review and update them; use filters to keep hardware-only policies off Cloud PCs.

units.title: Monitor Cloud PC usage, performance, and health
points: **Cloud PC utilization** (Devices > Cloud PC performance): time connected and last connection — find rarely used Cloud PCs to reclaim licenses.
**Connection quality** (Reports > Cloud PC overview): round-trip time, bandwidth, gateway, sign-in time, protocol, UDP utilization.
Connectivity health: Available or Unavailable; **Troubleshoot this connection** shows failed checks (domain join, trust, blocked URLs).
**Resource performance** score is based on CPU and RAM spike time; below baseline → consider a resize. Cloud PCs must be enrolled in Endpoint analytics.
Cloud PC monitoring is in preview — use with caution in production.

keyTerms.definition: Intune object that tells Windows 365 how to build Cloud PCs and for which Entra user group.
Seven days of continued access after a license or assignment change before deprovisioning.
Deletes the Cloud PC and rebuilds it from the current provisioning policy; user data is lost.
Recommended security settings for Cloud PCs covering Windows, Edge and Defender.
Purpose-built device that connects users directly to their Cloud PC and is managed with Intune.

tables.title: Cloud PC status values
rows: Usable, but a non-critical step failed
Licensed, but no provisioning policy assigned
Not enough licenses available in the tenant
License or assignment changed; 7 days of continued use
Grace period over; Cloud PC being removed and can't be restored
Provisioning didn't complete; review, fix and retry

remember: Licensed user has no Cloud PC → status **Not provisioned** means **no provisioning policy assigned**; **Pending** means **not enough licenses**.
Needs more CPU/RAM but keep data → **Resize**, not Reprovision.
Provisioning policy assignment → **user groups, no nesting**; bulk remote actions → **user groups** too.
Ending the grace period manually is **destructive** — the Cloud PC's OS and data are deleted.

selfCheck.q: A user is licensed for Windows 365 Enterprise and in an assigned group, but the group is nested in another group targeted by the policy. Why is no Cloud PC created?
selfCheck.a: Nested groups aren't supported for provisioning policy assignments; add the user to a directly assigned group.

selfCheck.q: A user's Cloud PC is consistently below the resource performance baseline because of RAM spikes. What do you do?
selfCheck.a: Review the device history in the Resource performance report and resize the Cloud PC to add resources.

selfCheck.q: You need to find Cloud PCs that haven't been used for weeks so you can reassign licenses. Which report do you use?
selfCheck.a: The Cloud PC utilization report, which shows total time connected and date last connected.

modules.title: Explore Azure Virtual Desktop
modules.learnSummary: Explore Azure Virtual Desktop architecture, compare it with Windows 365, and learn how host pools, session hosts, and scaling deliver virtualized Windows desktops and apps from Azure.
modules.tldr: Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) is a platform service: Microsoft runs the control plane (web, broker, gateway), you run the session host VMs, images, networking and profiles. Users reach desktops or RemoteApps through workspaces and application groups attached to pooled or personal host pools. Compared with Windows 365, AVD gives more control and multi-session density, at the cost of more operational ownership.
objectives: Describe Azure Virtual Desktop architecture, including the control plane and customer-managed resources
Compare Azure Virtual Desktop with Windows 365 to match each option to the right scenario
Explain how host pools, session hosts, and scaling plans deliver desktops and apps to users
keyPoints: **Control plane** (Microsoft): web service, broker, gateway, resource directory. **Data plane** (you): session host VMs, images, apps, networking, identity, profiles (often **FSLogix**).
Resource chain: **host pool** (session hosts) ← **application group** (desktop or **RemoteApp**) ← **workspace** (what users see in the **Windows App**).
**Pooled** host pools share session hosts (density, needs a roaming profile solution); **personal** host pools give each user a dedicated VM.
**Reverse connect**: session hosts connect outbound to AVD, so **no inbound RDP ports** are opened; **RDP Shortpath** adds direct UDP paths with TCP as fallback.
Load balancing (pooled only): **breadth-first** spreads sessions for performance; **depth-first** fills a host to its limit for cost savings.
**Autoscale scaling plans** power hosts on/off by schedule; one plan can cover several host pools, but each host pool uses **only one** plan; personal pools can hibernate or deallocate.
**Start VM on Connect** powers hosts on only when a user connects — lower idle cost, longer first connection.
Choose **AVD** for multi-session density, RemoteApp-only publishing or deep Azure/network control; **Windows 365** for 1:1 Cloud PCs and Intune-first simplicity.

units.title: Understand Azure Virtual Desktop architecture
points: Microsoft runs brokering and connectivity, so you don't build classic Remote Desktop Services roles.
Connection flow: **feed discovery** (Entra sign-in, workspace subscription) then **session connection** (brokered RDP).
Session hosts can be Microsoft Entra joined (cloud-first) or domain joined via AD DS or Microsoft Entra Domain Services.
Session hosts need outbound connectivity to AVD endpoints; ExpressRoute or site-to-site VPN support private paths.
Windows App replaces the earlier Remote Desktop clients.

units.title: Compare Azure Virtual Desktop with Windows 365
points: AVD: platform service, pooled multi-session and personal desktops, you design networking, managed in the Azure portal.
Windows 365: SaaS 1:1 Cloud PC (Frontline adds concurrent use), capacity follows licenses, Intune-centric.
Task/shift workers → AVD pooled or Windows 365 Frontline; knowledge workers → Windows 365; app-only publishing → AVD.
Developers/power users → Windows 365 or AVD personal; bursty demand → AVD pooled or Frontline.
Decide per workload, not per company; use team skills as a tie-breaker.

units.title: Examine host pools, session hosts, and scaling
points: Start from a consistent image so scaling and troubleshooting are predictable.
Management: **standard** (you manage VMs) or **session host configuration** (service-managed creation and updates; pooled only, preview).
**Drain mode** blocks new sessions on a host while existing ones finish — for patching, scale-in and rotation.
Scaling options: autoscale plans (predictable hours, spiky sign-ins), Start VM on Connect (occasional use), custom automation (special rules).

keyTerms.definition: Collection of session host VMs registered to AVD; pooled or personal.
VM running Windows and the apps that host user sessions.
Publishes either a full desktop or selected RemoteApps from one host pool.
User-facing container presenting one or more application groups in the client.
Session hosts keep outbound connections to AVD, so no inbound RDP ports are needed.
Stops new sessions landing on a host while existing sessions continue.
Powers on a session host only when a user connects.

tables.title: AVD vs Windows 365
rows: Platform: Microsoft control plane, you run hosts, images, network
SaaS Cloud PCs; Microsoft runs most infrastructure
Dedicated 1:1 Cloud PC; Frontline concurrent use
Scale host capacity by demand and schedules
Task workers, shared desktops, app-only publishing, bursty demand
Knowledge workers, steady usage, simple operations

tables.title: Breadth-first vs depth-first load balancing
rows: Fills one host to its max session limit first

remember: Publish one line-of-business app without a full desktop → **AVD RemoteApp** application group.
Users connect to **workspaces/application groups**, never directly to host pools.
Cost first → **depth-first**; performance first → **breadth-first** (pooled host pools only).
Each host pool can have **only one** autoscale scaling plan, though a plan can serve several host pools.

selfCheck.q: You need to patch a session host without kicking off active users. What do you use?
selfCheck.a: Drain mode, which prevents new sessions on that host while existing sessions finish.

selfCheck.q: A pooled host pool is rarely used outside office hours, and cost must be minimized. Which load-balancing algorithm and scaling option fit?
selfCheck.a: Depth-first load balancing combined with an autoscale scaling plan scheduled around office hours.

selfCheck.q: Does AVD require inbound RDP ports to be opened to the internet?
selfCheck.a: No. With reverse connect transport, session hosts keep outbound communication to the AVD service.

modules.title: Integrate Azure Virtual Desktop with Microsoft Intune
modules.learnSummary: Enroll Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts in Microsoft Intune, apply compliance and configuration policies, monitor and troubleshoot virtual desktops, and address governance, licensing, and hybrid scenarios.
modules.tldr: Enrolling Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts in Intune brings them under the same management plane as physical PCs and Cloud PCs: configuration, compliance, endpoint security, apps and updates. Windows Enterprise multi-session is supported but behaves differently — target device settings to device groups, expect some Not applicable results, and use the Settings catalog instead of update rings. Combine Intune reporting with Azure Virtual Desktop Insights, and plan governance and licensing for hybrid environments.
objectives: Enroll Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts in Microsoft Intune
Apply compliance and configuration policies to session hosts
Monitor and troubleshoot Azure Virtual Desktop environments
Address governance, licensing, and hybrid scenarios for Azure Virtual Desktop
keyPoints: Only **Windows 10/11 Enterprise multi-session** (and single-session client) session hosts enroll in Intune; **Windows Server session hosts can't** — use Configuration Manager or Group Policy.

Session hosts must be **Microsoft Entra joined** (recommended) or **hybrid Entra joined** and enroll through **automatic MDM enrollment**; hybrid joined multi-session uses **device credential enrollment**.
On multi-session, assign **device settings to device groups** and **user settings to user groups**; **compliance policies must target device groups**.
**Not applicable** is often expected on multi-session — build policies in the **Settings catalog** with an OS edition filter for Enterprise multi-session.
**Update rings aren't supported** on multi-session; configure Windows Update for Business settings through the **Settings catalog**.
Secure Boot/TPM compliance needs **Generation 2 VMs with Trusted Launch** — plan it at deployment, it can't be enabled on existing hosts.
**Intune** shows device compliance, policy and update health; **Azure Virtual Desktop Insights** (Azure Monitor + Log Analytics) shows sessions, connections and host performance.
Licensing: **Windows 365** per user, compute included; **AVD** uses an eligible license (e.g. Microsoft 365 E3/E5, Business Premium) **plus Azure consumption costs**.

units.title: Enroll Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts in Microsoft Intune
points: Benefits: consistent profiles and baselines, app deployment, Windows Update for Business, compliance, Defender and Conditional Access integration.
Workflow: deploy host → Entra join or hybrid join → automatic MDM enrollment (check the MDM user scope) → register → receive policies.
Verify under **Devices > Windows**: inventory, compliance, profile and endpoint security status, update reporting.
Validate profiles, baselines, apps and remediation scripts in a **pilot host pool** before production; use Azure Compute Gallery for images.

units.title: Apply compliance and configuration policies to session hosts
points: Personal (single-session) hosts behave like physical Windows Enterprise devices; pooled multi-session hosts may not support every setting.
Settings catalog is the recommended profile type; Administrative Templates remain useful for Group Policy–based settings.
Conditional Access evaluates the compliance of the device hosting the user session — validate designs for shared hosts.
Use endpoint security policies for Defender, firewall, ASR, BitLocker, EDR and account protection; test performance impact in a pilot pool.
Assign through dynamic device groups, separate pilot and production, host pool–specific groups.

units.title: Monitor and troubleshoot Azure Virtual Desktop with Microsoft Intune
points: Hosts not checking in → network, enrollment, Entra registration or service communication problems.
Profile issues: conflicts, unsupported settings, wrong assignment, device/user scope mismatch, connectivity, licensing.
Enrollment issues: MDM not triggered, outdated AVD agent, multiple MDM providers (loop), **cloned images with existing enrollment** (never supported).
Disable token roaming through FSLogix; apps should deploy in system context to device groups.
AVD Insights needs a Log Analytics workspace, data collection rules and diagnostic settings on host pool and session hosts.

units.title: Address governance, licensing, and hybrid scenarios
points: Hybrid estates mix Entra joined, hybrid joined, AVD, Windows 365, domain-joined and co-managed devices.
Governance domains: identity (Entra Connect Sync/Cloud Sync, CA, MFA, break-glass), device, security and operational governance.
Windows 365 Enterprise requires Intune licensing; Intune is included in Microsoft 365 E3/E5, Business Premium and EMS.
Separate admin roles (identity, endpoint, Azure, security, virtual desktop) with RBAC in Intune and Azure for least privilege.
Licensing changes over time — validate against official Microsoft licensing documentation.

keyTerms.definition: Windows client edition allowing multiple concurrent user sessions; supported by Intune with per-setting limitations.
Enrollment method required for hybrid Entra joined multi-session session hosts.
Generation 2 VM security feature providing Secure Boot and vTPM; must be chosen at deployment.
Azure Monitor/Log Analytics workbooks for session, connection and host performance monitoring.
Policy status when a setting isn't supported on the platform, common on multi-session hosts.

tables.title: Intune vs Azure Virtual Desktop Insights
rows: Host CPU, memory and disk utilization

tables.title: Windows 365 vs Azure Virtual Desktop licensing

remember: Windows Server session host won't enroll in Intune → **expected**; manage it with Configuration Manager or Group Policy.
Updates not deploying to multi-session hosts → you used **update rings**; use the **Settings catalog** instead.
Compliance on multi-session → **device groups only**; user-targeted compliance isn't supported.
Session host problem in **device config/compliance** → Intune; slow sessions or **connection failures** → AVD Insights.

selfCheck.q: Compliance requiring Secure Boot reports noncompliant on all existing AVD session hosts. What's the cause and fix?
selfCheck.a: The VMs weren't deployed as Generation 2 with Trusted Launch, which can't be enabled afterwards; redeploy hosts with Trusted Launch.

selfCheck.q: Newly deployed session hosts from a cloned, previously enrolled image fail to sync with Intune. Why?
selfCheck.a: Cloning already-enrolled devices isn't supported — duplicated enrollment tokens and identities cause failures. Images must not contain enrollment information.

selfCheck.q: Several settings in a profile show Not applicable on pooled hosts. What should you check first?
selfCheck.a: Whether those settings are supported on Windows Enterprise multi-session; rebuild the profile in the Settings catalog with the multi-session edition filter.
